articles.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 10
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint for the RB position in Week 10.
articles.body:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions . You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available .

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (vs. NE) - 134.5 proj. total yards

I'd keep starting Gibbs, personally. He's half PPR's all-time RB26 through the first eight games.

This week, the Lions are back to a 27.0-point team total (fourth) as 2.5-point home favorites against the Patriots, who struggled against THE Kaleb Johnson last week. New England is typically better, however, allowing just 17.1 half PPR points to RBs this year (28th). But it also hasn't faced Gibbs!

2. Kenneth Walker III (at ATL) - 111.5 proj. total yards

After a couple of mediocre games against top-end defenses, Walker predictably rebounded against the Jets. He's back to the RB2 on RB2 usage this season. In fact, Walker is half PPR's all-time RB34 through the first eight games.

The Falcons have been lit up against RBs recently with some injuries at EDGE and LB, allowing Bucky Irving (170 total yards), Christian McCaffrey (RB6) and D'Andre Swift (RB5) to run wild. They also just traded away S Jesse Bates this week. This is a potential big game with the Chiefs projected for 24.5 points as 3.5-point road favorites.

3. Christian McCaffrey (at DAL) - 98.5 proj. total yards

Since cramping in Australia, CMC is the RB3 on RB4 usage. Good reminder to touch grass instead of panicking based on a small sample.

This is an eruption spot against the Cowboys, of course. The 49ers have a 29.5-point team total in a game projected for 55.5 total points. Dallas has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to RBs this year, even allowing Tyler Allgeier to drop 191 total yards in Week 8. I expect Kyle Shanahan to toy with these Dallas LBs and Ss all game.

4. Bijan Robinson (vs. KC) - 118.5 proj. total yards

Bijan rebounded in Week 9 after the offense went away from him as a receiver in the month prior. His six receptions were really refreshing to see. He still handled 19 carries, too, with Brian Robinson Jr. on injured reserve. The Falcons traded away their starting C at the deadline as a sign of what this season is for Atlanta, but it's still a well-coached OL. Robinson is still in line to finish as a top-5 RB, as he's started the year as the RB4 on RB10 usage, even if it's been more volatile than we had hoped.

Kansas City is 28th in half PPR points allowed to RBs, while both the Falcons (44%, 30th) and Chiefs opponents (46%, 30th) sit in the bottom three in neutral pass rate. Atlanta enters with a 21.0-point implied team total (18th) as 3.5-point home underdogs. It's not a clean matchup for Robinson, but the game plan will be to let him attempt to take over.

5. James Cook III (at NYJ) - 103.5 proj. total yards

Cook has scored 16.7+ half PPR points in seven straight games. He's up to the RB5 on RB7 usage across this season, almost identical to how he placed last year. He's averaging 102 rushing YPG (RB3) on the second-most carries. Managing 107 rushing yards against the Vikings last week is the most recent feather in his cap.

This matchup is far, far easier. It's an eruption spot against the Jets, who are missing star DT T'Vondre Sweat (IR). They've allowed the seventh-most rushing YPG (128) and have drastic on/off splits with Sweat. Kenneth Walker III just finished as the RB1 overall against them last week, and Cook was the RB2 overall in Week 2 of last year against them. The Bills have the highest team total of the week (29.5).

6. Chuba Hubbard (at NO) - 103.5 proj. total yards

There have been some OL changes, and it'll be nice when star LG Damien Lewis returns, but Hubbard's role is extremely stable each week. He's cleared 12.7 expected half PPR points in 8-of-9 recent games, leading Hubbard to an RB6 on RB14 usage ranking. If you look up mid-range RB1 in the dictionary, Hubbard's face appears.

This is an eruption spot. The Saints have allowed the most schedule-adjusted fantasy points to RBs, allowing the RB room to add 26 more yards than usual. They've allowed 134 rushing YPG (fourth), despite Chase Young and Carl Granderson providing pass-rush juice at EDGE. It won't help that they traded away a DT this week. The Panthers project for 23.0 points (12th).

7. Javonte Williams (vs. SF) - 83.5 proj. total yards

Williams is continuing his RB8 season and will now have another backup behind him in Kendre Miller following Tyler Goodson's injury. Volume and goal-line chances are never a concern here, as he's the RB9 in carries, RB21 in receptions and the RB1 in inside-the-5-yard-line carries. He has three more carries at the goal line than anyone else in the league.

This week is no different. The Cowboys project for 26 points against the 49ers, and that game total of 55.5 points is one of the highest of the entire season. San Francisco lost one of its up-and-coming DTs recently, but Nick Bosa is back and DeForest Buckner was recently added. This is a better DL now than it was last month. The Niners already sit as the second-best defense in rushing YPG (80.9) this year, too. The good news is the Cowboys' OL had their best rushing performance of the year last week, leading to over 3.0 yards before contact. It's one of the best lines in the NFL quite easily, especially in run blocking.

8. Bhayshul Tuten (at TEN) - 83.5 proj. total yards

Tuten had his lowest usage of the year in Week 9 because the Jaguars rolled the Ravens and Tuten was legitimately questionable with an ankle injury. He's had extra time to heal and should be back to his usual fringe-RB1 self now. Tuten was the RB13 on RB18 usage removing last week, despite only being the RB39 in receptions per game. He's a big play and goal-line threat in a potent offense. It appears that Liam Coen trusts him a whole lot more now than before.

The Titans are a joke. They don't have superstar DT Jeffery Simmons and also traded away S Amani Hooker. They're on a 3-game streak of allowing the starting RB (Chase Brown, Quinshon Judkins and Jonathan Taylor) to clear 101+ total yards. Jacksonville hits the road as 10.5-point favorites with an implied team total of 28.5 points (third).

9. Derrick Henry (vs. LAC) - 87.5 proj. total yards

It's best to just throw out last week with Joe Fagnano. Henry has played in seven games without Lamar Jackson and Fagnano since the beginning of last year, and Henry is the RB5 on RB3 usage in them. That's the optimistic case with Jacoby Brissett coming in to settle things down. He'll be loaded up with carries as long as the game script allows for it.

The winless Chargers provide just that. The Ravens are 4.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 21.5 points (17th). Los Angeles has allowed 122 rushing YPG this year and just traded away LB1 Daiyan Henley and placed S1 Derwin James on IR. Henry's outlook is significantly better this week than last, especially with star first-round LG Vega Ioane and C Cam Jurgens in the lineup.

10. Kyren Williams (at ARI) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Williams is running poorly recently. Blake Corum is playing every other drive. That has been true for a very long time. The real drivers over this RB24 on RB23 usage month have been 1) bad TD luck and 2) the Rams not being as good as expected. Williams only has two touchdowns this month, while Corum has four. The Rams being unable to stretch the ball vertically in the pass game has led to fewer scoring drives in general (15th in scoring and 17th in EPA/play this month).

The latter is scarier for his fantasy RB1 status, as Matthew Stafford looks tiers worse on tape individually this year and now won't have either top WR for the next few weeks. Williams could see his receiving volume climb to counteract the loss of projected points, but his lower TD equity is impacting him.

The good news is the Cardinals are up next. Los Angeles has a 24.5-point implied team total (ninth) against one of the worst offenses I've seen on paper. Williams has finished as the RB24, RB20, RB9, RB9, RB21, RB1 and RB2 against Arizona throughout his career.

11. Jaylen Warren (at CIN) - 92.5 proj. total yards

Since Rico Dowdle returned, Warren is the RB10 on RB14 usage, seeing 58% of the carries. He's been the RB18 or better in usage every week since Week 3, while being one of the most efficient players. Only Kenneth Walker III is ahead of him in rushing yards over expected (+26%), and this Steelers OL deserves a lot of credit with C Zach Frazier playing like the best in the league. The amount of explosives he's generated is unsustainable, but Warren easily looks like an upside RB2 at the very least.

The Bengals have superstar DT Dexter Lawrence to account for, but their EDGE, LB and S groups have struggled to contain RBs. Bijan Robinson and Tony Pollard have posted RB3 overall finishes in back-to-back weeks against them. As the lead back in Week 3, Warren was the RB8 on 176 scoreless yards. (That was the sniper game that took away a touchdown from him, if you remember that.) Pittsburgh heads on the road as 3.5-point road underdogs with an implied total of 23 points (14th).

12. Jonathan Taylor (vs. MIA) - 85.5 proj. total yards

The trade deadline was not kind to Taylor. The Colts kept him, possibly with the idea being that they can trade him in the offseason and save some face as the rest of this season winds down. But they also traded away superstar LG Quenton Nelson, star DT DeForest Buckner, WR Josh Downs and WR Keenan Allen. This team is simply way worse now. This is how Taylor has finished, depending on how well his team has been over a huge sample:

The good news is the Dolphins are just as bad, especially with Malik Willis headed to IR now. Indianapolis enters as 3.5-point home favorites with an implied total of 21 points (19th).

The thing to watch for here is if Taylor is a 70% or 90% player with Seth McGowan flashing some potential as his backup. Last week's goal-line touchdown was due to Taylor unfortunately losing his shoe, but McGowan has mixed in before garbage time over the past month. That wasn't the case at the peak of Taylor's fantasy value. Taylor is the RB19 on RB13 usage this month.

13. Chase Brown (vs. PIT) - 71.5 proj. total yards

Brown had his second-lowest usage (9.0 expected half PPR points) of the season in last week's blowout win against the Falcons. This month, Brown is the RB39 on RB16 usage, handling RB35 carries and RB3 receptions per game. The lack of rushing production has really hurt him, particularly near the goal line. Here's what happened down there last week:

Brown is having a bad season and is holding onto RB2 value in the most optimistic angle solely because the Bengals are averaging 30.0 points (second).

Brown flipping the switch against a loaded Steelers defense would be a surprise, as they've allowed the third-fewest rushing YPG this year. They have at least allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to RBs via the receiving game (8.1 half PPR points). Offenses facing Pittsburgh have passed the ball in neutral situations at the highest rate (60%). Cincy is already leading in that metric (66%), so Brown saving face with 4-6 receptions wouldn't be surprising. The Bengals are 3.5-point home favorites with an implied total of 26.5 points (fifth).

14. Blake Corum (at ARI) - 66.5 proj. total yards

Corum is on fire. He's the RB14 on RB37 usage this month. The Rams have the RB1 and RB2 overall in rushing success rate right now, after also finishing there last season. They'll be RB-reliant here with both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams looking weeks away. Corum will continue to rotate drives with Kyren Williams, and whoever is on the field for their scoring drives will be the one to finish with the better outing. Corum's floor is about 12 carries without a target, so he's as TD-reliant as they get.

The good news is the Cardinals are bad. Los Angeles has a 24.5-point team total (ninth), and the Cardinals have allowed 122 rushing YPG this year. Corum was the RB14 with 60 yards and a score against them in Week 6 and was the RB26 and RB3, respectively, against them last season. To my surprise, Arizona didn't trade away any of its defensive starters at the deadline.

15. Woody Marks (at CLE) - 78.5 proj. total yards

In three games without David Montgomery, Marks hasn't broken out despite an increased workload. He's not very good, nor is the Texans OL, but he is still a positive regression candidate, assuming he'll continue seeing 20.0 touches per game, leading to RB18 usage.

The Browns are a fine defense, checking in the middle of the pack in most metrics. They've recently fallen off, allowing Audric Estimé (RB9), Jaylen Warren (RB10) and Tony Pollard (RB1) to finish as fantasy RB1s. Those aren't loaded offenses, either. Houston travels as 4.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 22 points (15th).

I'm falling for it again. Please save me.

16. Cam Skattebo (vs. WAS) - 61.5 proj. total yards

Skattebo was a full participant (hamstring) and should be ready for what could be a pretty large workload with Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR and Devin Singletary struggling last week. Skattebo handled 17 carries in Week 7 as the lead back, finishing as the RB7 due to some explosive runs.

The matchup is cleaner with the Commanders placing DTs DaRon Payne and Javon Kinlaw on IR. They'll crowd the line with extra bodies, but they don't have a ton of talent right now. Back in Week 5, Skattebo had 71 total yards against them, while Christian McCaffrey (RB2), Saquon Barkley (RB21) and Blake Corum (RB13) had big moments against them in part-time roles. The Giants have a 22.0-point team total (16th).

17. Ollie Gordon II (at IND) - 84.5 proj. total yards

Gordon is losing starting QB Malik Willis to injured reserve, prompting Kyle McCord to make his NFL debut. It could get ugly. Gordon has four games as the starter when the offense has scored 9-19 points, and he's averaged 10.9 half PPR points in them (RB18). Over the past month, Gordon is the RB23 on RB10 usage.

The Colts are tanking and have been gashed by opponents with DT DeForest Buckner being traded away. Javonte Williams (RB5) and Bhayshul Tuten (RB2) took advantage of this terrible LB group. Across the year, Indy is fifth-worst against fantasy RBs on the third-most rushing YPG (137). Miami travels as 3.5-point road underdogs with an implied total of 17.5 points (25th).

18. Breece Hall (vs. BUF) - 75.5 proj. total yards

Hall was the RB17 on RB16 usage in his return to the field against the Chiefs, who blew them out of the water immediately. Hall didn't play as many passing downs as expected, but he did show nice athleticism as a rusher (15 carries) and still managed to have three receptions.

In the red zone, Hall had a few carries to get the Jets to the 4-yard line, but Braelon Allen entered afterwards and played on all three of those goal-line snaps. They split short-yardage work otherwise. Hall can't afford to lose goal-line work if the hope is returning to top-15 fantasy RB status. The Jets have averaged 19.1 expected half PPR points to their RB room this season, and it's roughly a 60/40 split. Hall is a volatile RB2.

The matchup is more daunting up front than in the air against the Bills. Buffalo has breakout DT Deone Walker and EDGE Gregory Rousseau, and it's only allowed 92 rushing YPG (26th). New York projects for 21.0 points as big-time home dogs.

20. Tony Pollard (vs. JAX) - 70.5 proj. total yards

Pollard has been on a tear recently, sitting at RB7 in half PPR points per game on RB11 usage over his last four contests. He has cleared 115 rushing yards in consecutive games against the Browns and Bengals. Across the entire year, Pollard is the RB16 on RB16 usage. The Titans should be playing better ball after their bye, given how inexperienced the entire unit is.

Unfortunately, this is an impossible matchup. The Jaguars are only allowing 15.3 half PPR points to RBs this year on just 89 rushing YPG. They lost DT DaVon Hamilton, then traded for two DTs, including run-plugger Jordan Davis. They also added S Jesse Bates. Offenses facing Jacksonville have passed the ball the second-most often (59%) in neutral situations because of how dominant it is stopping the run. Tennessee enters as 10.5-point home underdogs with an implied total of 18 points (23rd). Pollard was the RB25 and RB47, respectively, against the Jaguars last year.

21. Corey Kiner (at DET) - 66.5 proj. total yards

Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is likely out a couple of weeks, and it's unclear if TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is going to make the trip to Germany. This assumes Henderson plays, but Kiner is the favorite for carries around the goal line. Even before Henderson's illness, Kiner was mixing in. He seems like the more obvious Stevenson replacement given his beef. The Patriots have averaged 18.2 expected half PPR points to their RB room this year (30th). It just depends on whether Kiner is going to get 50% or 75% of that work.

The matchup is pretty tough. The Lions are an obvious pass funnel, allowing the 25th-most rushing YPG (94) versus the most passing YPG (277). Detroit is missing LB Jack Campbell right now, but Kiner is at risk of getting game-scripted out given his complete nothingness as a receiver. The Patriots have a healthy 24.5-point team total (10th). He needs a touchdown.

22. Zach Charbonnet (at LV) - 74.5 proj. total yards

The coaching staff loves Charbonnet. That was evident given their celebrations on a stiff-arm run from the big fella. Unfortunately, they're ramping him up slowly and the high-value touches aren't necessarily there. He's played on 32% of passing-down snaps and on 4 of 9 snaps inside the 10-yard line. When they are at the inch line, they've used TE A.J. Barner as their goal-line option. Charbonnet has been the RB22 and RB19 in expected half PPR points since returning. He can be treated as an RB3/FLEX.

This matchup is a great one, even if Drew Lock is banged up at QB. The Raiders are allowing the most rushing YPG (150) and the third-most fantasy points to RBs at 24.1 half PPR points per game. CMC was the RB4 against them last week, while Braelon Allen (RB7), Kyren Williams (RB12) and James Cook III (RB3) extended this fantasy RB1 streak to beyond the past month. The Seahawks' 23.5-point team total is enough to hold out hope for a score here.

23. Ashton Jeanty (vs. SEA) - 64.5 proj. total yards

24. Rachaad White (at NYG) - 54.5 proj. total yards

White has been a totally fine FLEX play without Jacory Croskey-Merritt:

In a very difficult spot against Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, with backups on the OL, White survived as the RB26 while splitting time with Austin Ekeler. White is only seeing 8-14 touches per game but has mixed in at the goal line and when trailing bigly to hold onto fantasy relevance. The Commanders have a neutral outing with the Giants and DROY candidate Arvell Reese this time out. Bill was the RB17 on 82 yards against them in Week 5 when he was the starter.

25. Quinshon Judkins (vs. HOU) - 53.5 proj. total yards

26. Chris Rodriguez Jr. (at TEN) - 47.5 proj. total yards

Rodriguez isn't going to close the Bhayshul Tuten gap, but he is still splitting the goal-line role and occasionally ripping off an explosive himself. He's been the RB19 and RB18 in the most recent contests, as a TD-or-bust FLEX option in half PPR. He's still only the RB57 in usage across the season, so beware of chasing recency bias. Jacksonville has a massive 28.5-point team total against the Jeffery Simmons-less Titans. If there's a week to dream, it's this one. But that was also true over the past two outings against the Colts and Ravens with Joe Fagnano.

27. Rico Dowdle (at CIN) - 49.5 proj. total yards

Since returning, Dowdle has been the RB29, RB21 and RB26 in expected half PPR points while attempting to keep up with Jaylen Warren. The Steelers' OL is strong enough for both backs to be fantasy-viable, especially if Dowdle can sneak in a touchdown along the way. In a win against the Browns in Week 8 before the bye, Dowdle handled 15 carries, showcasing what his upside can be in positive game scripts.

Unfortunately, the Bengals are a pass-funnel defense and the Steelers are projected to lose by 3.5 points. It'd be surprising if Dowdle sees as many second-half carries in this one, and the scheme might lean towards Warren's receiving ability to get him matched up with these concerning LBs. That said, Dowdle can also break tackles against this group and the Steelers still have a 23-point team total here. It's a fine enough spot for Dowdle to have FLEX value in half PPR leagues.

28. Jadarian Price (at LV) - 59.5 proj. total yards

Price has back-to-back RB30 finishes in terms of usage, averaging 9.3 expected half PPR points in his two games with Zach Charbonnet back in the mix. Price is not starting, nor is he getting goal-line work. He's played 1 of 9 snaps inside the 10-yard line over this span. Where he's been helpful is as a receiver (four catches last week in a win) and on explosive designed runs. He'll need receptions and big runs to be fantasy-viable, and those are harder to get without LG Quenton Nelson. Hopefully LT Charles Cross is back here. Price is a no-floor FLEX in half PPR only.

The good news is the Raiders are pretty terrible! They've allowed the most rushing YPG (150), and the Seahawks have a healthy 23.5-point total as favorites against the debuting Fernando Mendoza.

29. Kaleb Johnson (vs. MIN) - 30.5 proj. total yards

31. Tyler Allgeier (vs. LAR) - 62.5 proj. total yards

We'll see if Bam Knight (concussion) returns.

32. Kaelon Black (at DAL) - 41.5 proj. total yards

33. Omarion Hampton (at BAL) - 39.5 proj. total yards

34. Alvin Kamara (vs. CAR) - 19.5 proj. total yards

35. Braelon Allen (vs. BUF) - 50.5 proj. total yards

Allen only handled eight carries and two receptions with Breece Hall back last week in a blowout loss. There was a moment where Hall brought the team inside the 5-yard line on back-to-back carries, and then Allen was subbed in for the remaining three snaps near the goal line. He was stuffed on one of those snaps (not his fault), potentially a sign that he could be a goal-line vulture. If that doesn't happen, then Allen can't be started, even in the FLEX. He only had 7.2 expected half PPR points last week.

Hopefully the Jets can keep this game against the Bills close. Throughout the year, opposing offenses have been pass-heavy against them. Buffalo has only allowed 92 rushing YPG (26th).

36. Dylan Sampson (vs. HOU) - 44.5 proj. total yards

37. Austin Ekeler (at NYG) - 42.5 proj. total yards

38. Devin Singletary (vs. WAS) - 35.5 proj. total yards

39. Aaron Jones Sr. (at GB) - 41.5 proj. total yards

40. Jordan Mason (at GB) - 47.5 proj. total yards

41. Emmett Johnson (at ATL) - 25.5 proj. total yards

42. Mike Washington Jr. (vs. SEA) - 29.5 proj. total yards

43. Justice Hill (vs. LAC) - 27.5 proj. total yards

44. Samaje Perine (vs. PIT) - 31.5 proj. total yards

45. Seth McGowan (vs. MIA) - 41.5 proj. total yards

47. Kimani Vidal (at BAL) - 31.5 proj. total yards

48. Keaton Mitchell (at BAL) - 24.5 proj. total yards

50. Pierre Strong (vs. MIN) - 11.5 proj. total yards

articles.title: Pista libre para Alcaraz y Jódar
articles.standfirst: Ambos españoles no tendrán que medirse en la primera fase de las ATP Finals y se multiplican las opciones de verlos en los cruces
articles.summary: Ambos españoles no tendrán que medirse en la primera fase de las ATP Finals y se multiplican las opciones de verlos en los cruces
articles.body: La temporada de la ATP llega a su fin y lo hace con pista libre para Carlos Alcaraz y Rafa Jódar. El sorteo celebrado en Turín ha deparado que los dos españoles no tendrán que enfrentarse entre sí durante la primera fase de las ATP Finals. Por tanto, se multiplican las posibilidades de ver a ambos en las eliminatorias por el título. Un escenario que alimenta la ilusión del tenis español en la última gran cita del calendario... con las mejores casas de apuestas muy atentas. Los caminos de ambos, eso sí, serán diferentes. Alcaraz, que perdió la final de la pasada edición frente a Jannik Sinner, tendrá que medirse a Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli y Frances Tiafoe. Por su parte, Jódar, que afronta su debut en el torneo, se verá las caras con Alexander Zverev, Ben Shelton y Arthur Fils. No hay margen para el error: en Turín se reúnen los ocho mejores tenistas de la temporada y cada partido exigirá el máximo nivel. Pese a la dificultad del desafío, Alcaraz parte como el gran favorito para levantar el trofeo. El murciano ha regresado de su lesión en un gran estado de forma y, además, tiene ganado el cara a cara frente a todos sus rivales en el torneo. Tonybet sitúa su cuota para conquistar las ATP Finals en 1.9. Una cifra que refleja la confianza en el español para cerrar el año con un nuevo título. Las apuestas deportivas le colocan por delante del resto de participantes. La situación de Jódar es muy diferente. Su cuota para proclamarse campeón asciende hasta los 11.01, sólo por delante de la de Fils, que alcanza los 13.01. Sin embargo, para el joven español ya supone un éxito mayúsculo estar entre los ocho mejores del curso. Lo que parecía inimaginable a principios de temporada se ha convertido en una realidad. Ahora, tratará de aprovechar la oportunidad para dar la sorpresa y alcanzar las semifinales. En ese camino, Zverev aparece como uno de los grandes obstáculos para Alcaraz y como uno de los principales aspirantes al título, con una cuota de 5.0 en Tonybet. Por detrás figura Shelton, con 7.01. El morbo está servido. Alcaraz y Jódar todavía no se han enfrentado en un partido oficial y el sorteo ha dejado abierta la posibilidad de que su primer duelo llegue en el escenario más importante: la final de las ATP Finals. articles.title: Ranking the Most Likely 2027 WWE Royal Rumble Men's and Women's Winners
articles.summary: The 2027 WWE Royal Rumble doesn't feel imminent with the John Cena Classic, Wrestlepalooza and Survivor Series still on the horizon. However, right now is when Superstars start building momentum toward a potential Rumble win.
articles.body:
The 2027 WWE Royal Rumble doesn't feel imminent with the John Cena Classic, Wrestlepalooza and Survivor Series still on the horizon. However, right now is when Superstars start building momentum toward a potential Rumble win.

As it stands, Sami Zayn and Roman Reigns will be walking into WrestleMania season with the Undisputed WWE Championship and World Heavyweight Championship, respectively, but anything can change between now and the beginning of the year.

While there might be one or two early favorites for both Battle Royals, there are any number of different directions WWE can realistically go. In fact, the overall lack of direction for the current product will help make outcomes more unpredictable.

WrestleMania 43 should boast a star-studded card in Saudi Arabia, so it's imperative WWE nails the main events. Various marquee matchups have been rumored, but it will be the results of the Rumbles that definitively determine what fans have to look forward to.

These are the best picks for the 2027 men's and women's Royal Rumble matches, ranked from least to most likely.

It hasn't been an overly productive 2026 for Gunther. He entered the year with the momentum of retiring John Cena and followed that up by retiring AJ Styles in January, only to find himself directionless during WrestleMania season and feuding with Nick Aldis and Danhausen.

Although he had multiple chances to win the Undisputed WWE Championship back in the spring, he came up short on every single occasion. He doesn't quite feel like the attraction he once was, but that doesn't mean he can't get back to that elite level with a simple Royal Rumble victory.

Gunther has had strong showings in the Rumble before, but this could be the year he goes all the way and wins the whole thing, setting himself up for a WrestleMania main event.

Iyo Sky finds herself in a similar spot where she's incredibly established and has picked up the occasional big win here and there in 2026 but isn't factored into any high-profile plans at the moment. She's also one Rumble triumph away from being a key player in the world title picture again.

Sky vs. Liv Morgan has been done to death over the last two years, but by WrestleMania 43, it's very possible that someone else will be in possession of the Women's World Championship.

Although Roman Reigns' road to WrestleMania 43 looks to be a lock, Jacob Fatu shouldn't be completely discounted as a potential opponent for him given their history.

In the immediate aftermath of WrestleMania 42, Fatu emerged as the first challenger to Reigns' newly won World Heavyweight Championship. He lost to The Tribal Chief at both Backlash and Clash in Italy, with the latter defeat forcing him to fall in line and reluctantly join The Bloodline.

Despite that, he's largely been on the same page as Reigns and The Usos for the last several months, aside from occasional hints of tension. That doesn't mean he and Reigns can't renew their rivalry, potentially at WrestleMania, where Fatu could finally beat him one-on-one.

Blake Monroe is a bit of a dark horse in her own right considering how much of a non-factor she's been on SmackDown since debuting on the main roster right after WrestleMania 42. It took her months to show up in person, and then another few months to wrestle her first televised match.

Her feud with Giulia proved that she's a world champion-caliber competitor, but it's more a matter of WWE putting her in a position to shine. She hasn't come close to challenging for a top title yet, but winning the women's Rumble match would afford her that elusive opportunity.

Bron Breakker appeared to be the odds-on favorite to win last year's men's Rumble match, especially after he pinned then-world heavyweight champion CM Punk in WarGames at Survivor Series.

He unsuccessfully challenged for the title on the first Raw of 2026, a loss that could have seamlessly set him up for a Royal Rumble win later that month. Instead, he was the first entrant eliminated—lasting only seconds.

Breakker is currently far removed from the main event scene, but he could reestablish himself as a rising star by winning the men's Rumble and righting that wrong in the process.

Unlike Breakker, Naomi hasn't been around for well over a year, but she should also be considered a potential pick for a Rumble win come Feb. 6. She announced she was pregnant in August 2025 and relinquished the Women's World Championship, so she has something to strive for once she's ready to return.

Seeing as how she gave birth back in March, it wouldn't be out of the question for her to be back by the Rumble, clinch the win and punch her ticket to WrestleMania 43.

Stars Who Could Make Shock Return at Survivor Series 😮

Regardless of whether it's been Raw or SmackDown, CM Punk has been a permanent fixture in the world championship picture since the summer of 2025. His most recent run with the Undisputed WWE Championship ended in September at the hands of Sami Zayn and he's struggled to get his rightful rematch for the title.

His loss to Kevin Owens on last week's SmackDown suggests that he won't be back in championship contention anytime soon, which would give him enough time between now and the Royal Rumble to work his way up the ladder again and earn another shot by winning the Rumble itself.

A Rumble win is one of the few things Punk has yet to accomplish in his iconic career, and if him facing Cody Rhodes is the bout WWE is building to for WrestleMania 43, it's more likely Punk wins the Rumble and Rhodes regains the gold before then as opposed to the other way around.

Meanwhile, it's egregious that Roxanne Perez lost the women's Money in the Bank Ladder match when she made more sense than anyone else involved to take home the briefcase. She's been treading water since then even though there's a story to be told with her and Liv Morgan.

After being the MVP in previous Rumbles, 2027 could be the year The Prodigy finally has her hand raised in victory to kick off her long-awaited rivalry with Morgan over the Women's World Championship.

Coming out of his one-sided squash win over Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 42, Oba Femi should have been fast-tracked toward the World Heavyweight Championship and won it by SummerSlam.

He did wind up winning the King of the Ring tournament that in theory made him the number one contender, but he subsequently threw the title shot away so he could face Lesnar inside Hell in a Cell instead.

There's been no mention of Femi being owed a shot at the belt since then, so one would have to assume that he has to start from scratch and earn a title shot some other way. Emerging victorious from the men's Rumble would be his best bet, especially since tossing him over the top rope would be a tall task for anyone involved.

Femi will challenge for a top title at WrestleMania 43 regardless of how he gets there, but him winning the Rumble appears to be the most logical path.

The same can be said for Rhea Ripley, who abruptly disappeared from WWE TV in the spring after suffering an injury and ultimately vacated the WWE Women's Championship she had just won at WrestleMania 42. Her absence has been felt on SmackDown, but once she's cleared to compete, she'll be gunning for the title she was never beaten for.

Tiffany Stratton is fresh off cashing in Money in the Bank to become WWE women's champion, so Stratton vs. Ripley should be the play for 'Mania.

The Eradicator is no stranger to winning the women's Rumble, so while it won't sit well with everyone, the excitement over her being back should offset most of that fan fatigue.

articles.title: The Most Dominant Video Game Athletes of All Time, Ranked
articles.summary: Nothing hits quite like video game nostalgia, especially when it comes to overpowered athletes and characters whose reputations endure long after their games go out of fashion.
articles.body:
Nothing hits quite like video game nostalgia, especially when it comes to overpowered athletes and characters whose reputations endure long after their games go out of fashion.

We've all got stories. That one kryptonite character who, no matter what you try, puts the TV at serious risk of receiving a controller flush through its screen.

As such, let's use this as a safe space. A place to reminisce, unjudged, about the most unstoppable sports video game characters of all time.

Forget The Rock; it's The Undertaker who should be known as The Final Boss after the hell he put players through in WWE 2K14.

Six months before The Deadman's 21-0 WrestleMania streak ended, 2K devs unleashed "Defeat the Streak" on the world. It pitted players against a version of The Phenom that was essentially programmed to cheat. He could reverse the unreversible, used supernatural tricks to get ahead and would eat finishers like modern-day Roman Reigns.

He could only be faced on a souped-up Legend difficulty, a realisation that had the internet's sneakiest players literally changing his move set to make things easier.

Sometimes, pettiness needs to be admired.

Mark Turmell was not an NBA star of the 1990s. He was, in fact, NBA Jam's lead designer. A man whose game couldn't feature Michael Jordan because the Chicago Bulls icon opted out of the league's group licensing agreement to control his own image rights.

Turmell, a huge Detroit Pistons fan, thus decided to design the game's code so Bulls players would miss game-winning shots against his beloved team.

He was also available to unlock as a playable character using the code "MJT," entering the court with unbelievable stats, which just so happened to be led by ridiculous dunking skills.

If you know one thing about Adriano in PES 6, I guarantee it's this: 99 shot power.

The Brazilian footballer was enjoying his best career spell with Inter Milan at the time of the game's release in 2006. Konami put his best stats in exactly the right places to create a one-man wrecking machine that totally outshone the player in real life.

Adriano's maxed-out shot power was reinforced with 90 acceleration and 98 balance, essentially making him too quick to catch and too strong to knock down.

While his career didn't go the way many expected—Adriano retired 10 years ago after barely making 10 appearances across his last five clubs—the legend lives on to this day. Even through music .

And yes, FIFA/EAFC fans, we know about Claudia Pina, Victor Ibarbo and your endless cohort of OP stars. Adriano stands tall as the one.

Look at his face. Nintendo made him so punchable, yet why couldn't you hit him?! WHY IS HE STILL STARING?

Matt is the final boss in Wii Sports' super-not-serious-but-I'm-going-to-cry-soon boxing minigame. He pretends to be your friend. He's your coach. Your Mickey. LIES.

Before long, the champion boxer is whacking you in the face and reading every return shot like he's in The Matrix.

The fool even showed up in Wii Sports Resort as Swordplay champ a couple of years later. Matt's memeness has endured, much like his pristine, cold-blooded face, which barely has a scratch on it.

Remember watching Jon Dowd slug home run after home run on TV? You know… the Jon Dowd? No?

Better known as San Francisco Giants legend Barry Bonds, old JD was the powerhouse stand-in for Bonds when he declined to participate in the MLBPA's licensing agreement (somewhat of a theme for the top athletes on this list).

Dowd was an assistant producer at EA Sports whose name would go on to become synonymous with overpowered athletes in video games. Bonds put together his best season in 2004, elevating Dowd's stats to 99 power and 99 contact against right-handers.

Although he looked absolutely nothing like Bonds, the exact same date of birth, weight and height made it obvious he was modelled on one of the sport's best.

So good that friends often agreed to ban him.

Jeremy Roenick wasn't actually the highest-rated player on NHL '94, but he was the symbolic beneficiary of a coding quirk that took his already excellent stats and accidentally elevated them to god-tier.

The Chicago Blackhawks star flaunted a combination of pace and shooting power that would make him lethal in normal circumstances.

In the Sega Genesis version, a programming mistake known as the " weight bug " made lighter players harder to knock down while allowing them to deliver disproportionately powerful checks—an ideal advantage for Roenick.

You know you've got a problem when you're against a man who is the final boss in a game named after him. It's even worse when that man just so happens to be the scariest boxer in history.

There are plenty of reasons why Mike Tyson regularly makes it onto toughest-video-game-boss lists, even without the sport filter.

His uppercuts utterly destroy player-controlled character Little Mac in the opening round. He starts to fade if you survive the onslaught, but then begins to add more variety to his barrage of shots, including blink-and-you'll-miss-it jabs that will have you in serious danger.

Speaking of blinking, if you see Iron Mike momentarily close his eyes in Punch-Out!!, you better get the hell out of the way.

Good luck thinking of a nickname that is more badass than "The Secret Weapon." It certainly beats having to play baseball with "Cheese" or "Stinky Phil" in the schoolyard.

Pablo Sanchez's brilliance is very simple to understand. In the original Backyard Baseball, he had maximum ratings in batting, running and fielding, making him an extraordinary all-round player.

"Stood tall" might be the wrong turn of phrase. Sanchez was tiny! That only further added to his brilliance, making his strike zone much smaller for pitchers to hit. Never mess with the small kid.

"Bo Jackson and Steve Young in one body" is quite the way to describe Michael Vick in Madden NFL 2004. That's how EA explained Vick's design to the man himself, a virtual god who put the term "cheat code" into modern gaming nomenclature.

Vick simply had it all. Speed: 95. Agility: 95. Acceleration: 94. Throwing power: 97. Stamina: 95. What on earth are you meant to do to stop that? It's a question EA quickly tried to answer.

The Atlanta Falcons great's impact was so massive that the devs introduced the "Hit Stick" a year later. They also placed Ray Lewis on the front cover, perhaps as a defensive antidote to the lifetime of mental scars caused by those who were exposed to taking Vick on.

The average Bo Jackson run in Tecmo Bowl looks like the moment when Bryan runs down the street in Zach Cregger's new Resident Evil movie. There are bodies flying everywhere. Pure carnage, and no hope that the greatest virtual athlete in gaming history would ever be caught.

The phrase "he's running laps around them" is often said in jest. Not when it comes to Bo in Tecmo Bowl. He was literally too fast for the game, to be fair. His zig-zagging ability was so unstoppable that Rickon used it for inspiration during The Battle of the Bastards in Game of Thrones (probably).

Perhaps Quagmire said it best in Family Guy : "You're not really good, you've just got Bo Jackson."

articles.title: B/R NHL Staff Debates the Best Trade and Free-Agent Landing Spot for Nikita Kucherov
articles.summary: It appears that Nikita Kucherov's days in Tampa are numbered.
articles.body:
It appears that Nikita Kucherov's days in Tampa are numbered.

The reigning Hart Trophy winner has stated his intention not to re-sign in Florida come July 1. It's a blow for the Lightning, and losing Kucherov to either a trade or free agency would undoubtedly set the franchise back.

While the Bolts wrestle with the thought of losing one of the best players in franchise history, we here at B/R are thinking forward: What's the best place for Kuch going forward?

The B/R NHL staff got together to debate the best place for the Russian star. Disagree with our teams? Submit your thoughts now in the comments section of the app.

The Lightning are only trading Kucherov if they have no choice, and if they do, I doubt Montreal—a division rival whom they're likely to meet in the playoffs in the next few years—is at the top of their desired trade partners.

Montreal is an incredible landing spot for Kucherov nonetheless. He's extremely proud. The ultimate hockey city would appeal to someone who embraces big moments and has something to prove.

The Habs may not have a true franchise center in the vein of Crosby or MacKinnon, but Nick Suzuki is quite like a younger Brayden Point. Kucherov could work magic with some of their talented stars like Cole Caufield and Lane Hutson. Compatriot Ivan Demidov would be hard-pressed to find a better mentor.

The Habs, who had their building blocks already signed to team-friendly deals, can afford to throw a blank check at Kucherov without unbalancing their books. They have both NHL-ready talent and prospects to pull off a move for a star player (we know they're trying with Dylan Larkin).

So suppose Tampa GM Julien BriseBois learns that Kucherov was not throwing a temporary tantrum, but is 100 percent set on a new chapter, and that he will be joining the Canadiens one way or another. Are they really willing to lose arguably the best player in franchise history for nothing?

The competitive window remains open, but they're not a team swimming in resources. They've had to scrape together what they can from late-round picks and undrafted free agent signings in order to build a youth movement.

Can the Lightning reframe this in the way that Carolina parlayed Rantanen into assets? That sounds better than the alternative.

After several years of rebuilding under general manager Bill Armstrong, the Utah Mammoth emerged as a playoff contender last season. Adding Nikita Kucherov would help them take a big step toward Stanley Cup contention.

Armstrong spent those years drafting and developing young talent. However, he also made several bold moves in the trade and free-agent markets during the past two years, acquiring defensemen Mikhail Sergachev and MacKenzie Weegar and forwards Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck.

Landing Kucherov would be his biggest move yet, and his club has what it takes to make it happen.

Kucherov would be reunited with countryman and former Lightning teammate Sergachev. The Mammoth have one of the league's deepest prospect pools to use as trade bait. They also have over $12.2 million in accrued cap space at the trade deadline, and over $24 million projected for 2027-28.

The Mammoth have the assets and the cap space to absorb the remainder of Kucherov's cap space and the Lightning's asking price in the trade market, and the cap room next season to sign him via free agency next July.

Questions remain about the caliber of the Mammoth's goaltending and their overall defensive game. Nevertheless, having an established superstar like Kucherov skating alongside rising stars such as Clayton Keller and Logan Cooley would make them a force to be reckoned with in the Western Conference.

When it comes to where Nikita Kucherov goes next, it's been easy enough to single out the usual teams and cities, and even though Dallas might be considered one of them, their impending free agency with Jason Robertson has taken up all the attention. So we know what you're thinking: trade Robertson for Kucherov, right?

Wrong. Sign both of them and go wild on the rest of the league.

If the Stars get a long-term deal done with Robertson, the AAV will be in the stratosphere. The question is whether they commit to the maximum seven-year term. Considering he already makes $12 million this season, retaining him could require a relatively modest increase in their payroll compared with the cost of adding Kucherov.

Paying Robertson more while also finding room for Kucherov would still be a significant financial commitment. But Tyler Seguin's contract expires after this season, freeing up his $9.85 million cap hit and making it easier to accommodate both players.

If Kucherov isn't traded during the season—a possibility given Tampa Bay is a Stanley Cup contender—the real race will be to acquire his rights in the offseason and come up with an offer that makes him feel respected.

If Stars GM Jim Nill doesn't fear playing a potential game of chicken and hoping the star winger isn't traded, the offseason could see him keep one elite winger long-term and bring in another to go over the top with talent.

Some guys just look cringey in certain sweaters—Wayne Gretzky with the Blues, Mark Messier with the Canucks, Bobby Orr with the Blackhawks.

After all, his No. 86 has been a staple in Tampa Bay blue and white almost since the moment the Lightning made him the 58th pick of the 2011 draft—save for a 16-game stint wearing No. 56 at the outset of his 2013-14 rookie season.

And with all due respect to the colors worn by Montreal, Utah, Dallas, and others, given the two MVPs, three scoring titles, and two Stanley Cups Kucherov has earned since hitting the ice at the arena formerly known as the Tampa Bay Times Forum, there are simply no other threads that warrant his seven-time All-Star attention.

Is it possible someone makes GM Julien BriseBois an offer he can't refuse between now and the March 1 trade deadline, thus mandating that "Kuch" get a new stylist? Sure.

Connor Hellebuyck wanted a trade and got one. Brady Tkachuk wanted a trade and got one. Dylan Larkin wants a trade and could get one any day.

But it seems different with Kucherov, because the issues he's got are solvable.

Unlike those others, he's not frustrated by not winning. The Lightning have done plenty of that. And given a .722 points percentage through 18 games, they're probably not done.

Instead, he's frustrated by what he perceives as poor communication and a lack of respect from management. These are the sorts of issues that tend to fade when a team sits atop the standings, and its brass finally agrees to open the checkbook.

Unlike Steven Stamkos, who was exiled in summer 2024, Kucherov, despite turning 34 next year, deserves a significant raise from the $9.5 million annual cap hit he has carried since 2019-20. BriseBois knows that.

And, lest we forget, Tampa Bay is projected to have better than $28 million in wiggle room when the salary cap climbs past $113 million next season.

So, given the available money, his familiarity with the surroundings, and the upward mobility of the team, there's simply no place that makes more sense for Kucherov than staying put and signing a deal that'll allow him to retire with the franchise that drafted him.

articles.body: India enjoyed a highly successful campaign at the 2026 ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Doha, Qatar, finishing with 13 medals, including two gold, seven silver and four bronze. More importantly, the Indian shooting contingent secured three quota places for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, underlining the country's growing strength across different shooting disciplines.India finished second in the overall medal standings, behind China, who topped the table with 27 medals (13 gold, six silver and eight bronze). The Republic of Korea secured third place with 10 medals.Three Olympic quotas secured for LA28India's Olympic quota tally began with Jaypal Malviya, who won silver in the men's 10m air pistol event on November 5. His performance secured India's first quota place for the Los Angeles Games.Niraj Kumar added the second quota on November 11 after winning bronze in the men's 50m rifle 3 positions event. He also helped India claim bronze in the team competition alongside Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar and Akhil Sheoran.Vivaan Kapoor completed India's quota collection with a silver medal in the men's trap event on November 12. The Jaipur shooter finished level with Kuwait's Abdulrahman Alfaihan at 29 hits in the final but narrowly missed out on gold after losing the shoot-off 3-2.The three performances gave India quota places in men's 10m air pistol, men's 50m rifle 3 positions and men's trap, providing an important boost to the country's preparations for LA28.Two gold medals highlight India's campaignIndia's first gold medal came in the men's 50m pistol team event, where Ravinder Singh, Saurabh Chaudhary and Amanpreet Singh combined to finish on top of the podium.The women's 25m pistol team then delivered India's second gold medal. The trio of Esha Singh, Manu Bhaker and Divya Thadigol Subbaraju produced a combined score of 1761-68x to claim the title, finishing ahead of the Republic of Korea and Vietnam.Esha led the Indian team with 590-25x, while Manu contributed 587-24x and Divya added 584-19x.Indian shooters deliver across individual and team eventsIndia's silver-medal tally included several notable performances. Jaypal Malviya's podium finish in the men's 10m air pistol and Vivaan Kapoor's achievement in men's trap were among the standout results.Ravinder Singh also won individual silver in the men's 50m pistol, while India's women's 10m air rifle team of Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Shambhavi Kshirsagar finished second.The women's 10m air pistol team also secured silver, while Niveditha Veloor Nair won bronze in the women's 25m standard pistol individual event and helped India claim a team silver in the same discipline.India added further medals through Ankur Goel, who won individual silver in the men's 25m centre fire pistol and combined with Amanpreet Singh and Rajkanwar Singh Sandhu to secure team bronze.The men's 50m rifle 3 positions team of Aishwary, Akhil and Niraj also contributed a bronze medal, while the women's 25m pistol team's gold provided another major highlight.Full list of India's 13 medals at ISSF World Championships 2026EventMedalIndian shooter(s)Men's 50m Pistol TeamGoldRavinder Singh, Saurabh Chaudhary, Amanpreet SinghWomen's 25m Pistol TeamGoldEsha Singh, Manu Bhaker, Divya Thadigol SubbarajuMen's 50m Pistol IndividualSilverRavinder SinghWomen's 10m Air Rifle TeamSilverElavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar, Shambhavi KshirsagarWomen's 10m Air Pistol TeamSilverManu Bhaker, Suruchi Inder Singh, SainyamMen's 10m Air Pistol IndividualSilverJaypal MalviyaWomen's 25m Standard Pistol TeamSilverNiveditha Veloor Nair, Manvi Jain, Simranpreet Kaur BrarMen's Trap IndividualSilverVivaan KapoorMen's 25m Centre Fire Pistol IndividualSilverAnkur GoelWomen's 25m Standard Pistol IndividualBronzeNiveditha Veloor NairMen's 50m Rifle 3 Positions TeamBronzeAishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Akhil Sheoran, Niraj KumarMen's 50m Rifle 3 Positions IndividualBronzeNiraj KumarMen's 25m Centre Fire Pistol TeamBronzeAnkur Goel, Amanpreet Singh, Rajkanwar Singh SandhuGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NHL Trade Rumor: Lauren Kyle’s latest Toronto Maple Leafs promotion reignites speculation surrounding Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid
articles.summary: Lauren Kyle's recent promotion of Toronto Maple Leafs apparel through her fashion brand Sports Club Atelier sparks renewed speculation about Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid potentially moving to his hometown team.
articles.body: Connor McDavid has found himself back in Toronto Maple Leafs chatter, but this time it’s because of his wife, Lauren Kyle McDavid. Rather than a trade report, Lauren recently promoted Toronto Maple Leafs-branded apparel through her fashion label, Sports Club Atelier, prompting reactions from hockey fans across social media.The promotion attracted particular attention because of the long-standing speculation connecting Connor McDavid with his hometown franchise. Lauren also made it clear that the appearance was related to her brand's merchandise promotion, rather than a suggestion that the Edmonton Oilers captain was preparing for a move to Toronto. Kyle McDavid’s Toronto Maple Leafs apparel promotion sparks NHL rumorLauren Kyle McDavid's Toronto Maple Leafs apparel promotion generated fresh NHL discussions after fans noticed her modelling team-branded clothing on Instagram. The appearance quickly attracted attention because of her connection to one of hockey's biggest stars.Lauren Kyle models Toronto Maple Leafs gear for her fashion brand Sports Club Atelier, which produces hockey-themed and team-branded clothing. The promotion brought the Toronto franchise into conversations involving Connor McDavid, despite no direct connection to an official roster development.How did Toronto Maple Leafs fans react to the promotion?The video generated mixed reactions from Toronto Maple Leafs fans. As some fans saw the promotion as a humorous nod to their longtime desire for Connor McDavid to play for his hometown team.The reactions also demonstrated how quickly seemingly unrelated developments can generate NHL trade discussions when they involve prominent players.
