articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 10 Fades and Busts: Tony Pollard's hot streak gets extinguished
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Matt Okada sheds light on players we should temper expectations for in Week 10.
articles.body:
Welcome to the 10th of 17 weekly articles spotlighting the fantasy fades of the week! I am your host, Matt Okada, and I'll be bringing you half a dozen potential busts each and every Friday, from now until fantasy championships.

As a note, just because a player earns a "fade" or "bust" designation doesn't automatically mean they should be benched — it depends on the rest of your roster or the options on your waiver wire. But you can expect them to fall short of expectations (when I get them right). I include a "What to Do" section for every player to help with that.

Without further ado, here is my list for Week 10 of the 2026 season.

QB Matthew Stafford, Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals

Things have fallen apart quickly for Matthew Stafford and the Rams offense with the loss of Davante Adams late in Week 6 and the loss of Puka Nacua late last Sunday. The reigning MVP has not finished higher than QB12 in any week without Adams this season, and roughly half of his yards and touchdowns have gone to those two wide receivers in combination. Starting in Week 10, he'll be playing with both receivers absent for the first time since early 2024, when he averaged 8.5 fantasy points per contest over a four-game stretch, with just two touchdowns and three interceptions.

Without Adams' ability to separate, particularly in the red zone, or Nacua's ability to create tough catches and yards out of thin air, Stafford is left with very few reliable options moving forward (no disrespect to Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield). After consecutive outings with fewer than 13 fantasy points — including just 12.22 points against an extremely soft Commanders defense — it's hard to imagine him being more productive without Nacua, regardless of matchup. So while the Cardinals are probably "bright green" against quarterbacks in your fantasy app, I fear Stafford is a trap this week and I would look to stream a QB instead.

What to do ❓ Don't play Stafford (outside of 2QB leagues) if you can find any reasonable streaming alternative. That includes names like Tyler Shough, Bryce Young and C.J. Stroud (whom I actually love as a QB1 moving forward).

RB Ashton Jeanty, Las Vegas Raiders vs. Seattle Seahawks

On one hand, this feels bold. Fade Ashton Jeanty, a second-round fantasy pick who's been the RB17 in points per game? On the other hand, it also feels expected, following the trend of Jeanty's season into a matchup with the Seahawks. From Week 1 through Week 8, Jeanty's carry count stayed equal or dropped lower every single successive game and, when it bumped back up for the first time in Week 9, it was from two carries to six.

Since Week 5, he's tied for 51st among running backs in carries per game (with Corey Kiner) and 64th in rushing yards per game (behind, unironically, Sione Vaki). Jeanty's producing the entirety of his dwindling fantasy value through receiving, with at least three catches in every outing, 35+ receiving yards in seven of nine games and three of his four touchdowns coming through the air. Unfortunately, everything gets tougher against the Seattle defense, especially with a rookie quarterback in Fernando Mendoza making his debut start. Vegas is tied for the second-lowest implied total on the week (17 points) behind only the Cardinals (the other team with a rookie QB debut against a tough defense), and the 'Hawks are allowing the eighth-fewest receiving yards per game to running backs.

Even if Jeanty manages six or seven catches for 50 to 60 yards, he's still on a collision course with single-digit fantasy points. It's hard to sit him, I get it, but it was hard to sit Derrick Henry last week on TNF — and that was the right move.

What to do ❓ Jeanty slides out of RB2 range for me this week, so if you have decent depth and can turn to backs like Zach Charbonnet, Blake Corum, Woody Marks (if healthy) or even Corey Kiner ... strongly consider it.

RB Tony Pollard, Tennessee Titans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

I have to imagine that Pollard's 62.2 fantasy points in his last two games entering this week are the most for any player to crack this column in its history. Yes, he was revelatory in Weeks 7 and 8 against the Browns and Bengals. He averaged 5.4 yards per carry and scored five touchdowns in those two weeks, for 1.15 fantasy points per opportunity. But let's exercise some prudence here. Through the first six weeks , Pollard had logged just 4.0 yards per carry, scored just one touchdown and averaged 0.47 points per opportunity, dead last among qualified players. Can we really trust that drastic of a two-week breakout for the 29-year-old running back in the Titans offense?

I'm hesitant ... especially this week against Jacksonville. Entering the trade deadline, the Jaguars had allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs (15.3), with just 68.3 rushing yards per game (also second-fewest) and just four touchdowns in eight games. Then, they significantly strengthened their defense with the acquisitions of DTs Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux and safety Jessie Bates III. One of the other teams tied with the Raiders for second-lowest implied total this week is, unsurprisingly, the Titans. That's even worse for Pollard than it was for Jeanty, and I think the Tennessee RB comes crashing back down to earth this Sunday.

What to do ❓ You'll likely see Pollard projected and ranked quite highly around the industry ... I've got him right in Jeanty's range in half-PPR (outside the top 24), which means you can pivot to the same group of names mentioned above.

WR DK Metcalf, Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals

Frankly, DK Metcalf has been one of the most annoying and unpredictable calls in all of fantasy from week to week this season. He's hit double-digit fantasy points three times — just barely in Week 3, thanks to a touchdown — but fewer than seven points in every other game. His best performances came against the Browns and Buccaneers, theoretically tougher matchups for receivers, and then in the rematch with the Browns, he caught one pass for four yards. A big part of the problem is that he sees significant target volume but is usually horribly inefficient with that volume. He's one of 16 wideouts averaging 8+ targets per game but has scored just 7.7 fantasy points per game on those targets ... while every other receiver on that list has averaged 10+ PPG.

His 51.6% catch rate and 5.9 yards per target are both dead last on that list as well, and his 0.94 fantasy points per target is the lowest among 64 wideouts with more than 30 targets this season. At this point, I'm convinced the inefficiency is the expectation for Metcalf, rather than an opportunity for a breakout. He'll likely see solid volume against the Bengals — although he only had five targets in their first meeting — but the way he's played so far in 2026, he needs double-digit targets to approach double-digit fantasy points. I'd prefer a player with a higher floor, even on fewer expected opportunities.

What to do ❓ Metcalf is sort of the Jeanty of wide receivers — he slides out of WR2 range for me this week and I'd prefer "streamier" plays like Jalen Coker, DeMario Douglas, Omar Cooper Jr. or either Browns rookie.

WR Tre Tucker, Las Vegas Raiders vs. Seattle Seahawks

Tre Tucker has done just enough, just often enough, to keep himself in the fantasy starter conversation week to week this season. That ride includes 18+ fantasy points in three games … but it also includes fewer than eight fantasy points in the other six games, including a doughnut two weeks ago against the Jets. And in Week 10, that ride will be as bumpy as it gets. Not only are the Raiders starting rookie Fernando Mendoza in his NFL debut — after trading a productive Kirk Cousins at the deadline — but they're doing it against the Seahawks. Seattle's defense has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to wide receivers in 2026, with a league-low 99.6 receiving yards per contest and 6.2 yards per target.

They've also been particularly tough against downfield throws — where Tucker sees the vast majority of his targets — allowing the lowest yards per target, catch rate, success rate and EPA per play on those throws. And, unsurprisingly, they've surrendered the lowest explosive pass rate in the league, at just 10.1%. Nothing about this game instills confidence in Tucker and his occasional shot at a big fantasy day — barring a lucky breakaway play, expect another game with fewer than eight fantasy points.

What to do ❓ Tucker is already a volatile FLEX option week-to-week, but between Mendoza and the Seahawks secondary, he's outside the top-40 wide receivers and should not crack any reasonable redraft (or DFS) lineup.

TE Tucker Kraft, Green Bay Packers vs. Minnesota Vikings

Last week, I tagged Dalton Kincaid as the tight end fade against Minnesota and he ended up with just 4.3 fantasy points on three catches on Monday Night Football. While Tucker Kraft might feel like a slightly better tight end in a vacuum, he's also extremely risky against this Vikings defense. They've allowed just 3.9 receptions and 7.4 fantasy points per game to tight ends, both the fewest in the league, with just one touchdown in eight games. The 57.4% catch rate they've surrendered to the position isn't just the lowest in the league this season; it's the lowest for any defense in any of the last four seasons.

It also doesn't inspire confidence that Kraft is coming off his worst game of the year, with just one catch against the Patriots, a game in which he accounted for just an 11% target share and 0.3% of Jordan Love's 372 passing yards. And while Kraft's 8.0 points against this unit in Week 1 are actually the second-most by any tight end they've faced, no one has yet hit double digits and strong options like Sam LaPorta (5.0) and Colston Loveland (0.8) have been busts in this matchup as well.

It's hard to sit a regular TE1 in fantasy, but Kraft is on the absolute fringe this week.

What to do ❓ The most reasonable "streaming" name you can confidently start over Kraft is Hunter Henry — whom I love against the Lions — but if you happen to have someone like Kincaid, Brenton Strange or possibly even Darren Waller, give it some thought.

articles.title: NHL Indicates Finland's Block on Russian Athletes Could Affect Future Games There
articles.summary: The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in future, the league told The Associated Press.
articles.body:
The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in future, the league told The Associated Press.

Finland and Norway both announced plans to refuse entry to Russian athletes Thursday, the same day as the Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken played the first of two NHL regular-season games in the Finnish capital, Helsinki.

The Finnish restrictions take effect from Monday, after the NHL games, and follow a backlash to Russia being reinstated in the hockey world championships, which is not an NHL event.

"We are aware of the government's position and we'll have to take that into account," the league said on Friday when asked if the new restrictions would be an obstacle to future games in Finland.

The Finnish foreign ministry's statement outlining the restrictions didn't distinguish between Russian athletes on national teams, those competing as neutral athletes, or those on club teams in sports like hockey or soccer.

The ministry said Thursday that Russians would only be allowed to work in Finland on "tasks that are essential to Finland's national interests." It added that Russia "uses sports as a propaganda tool."

The NHL has played regular-season games in Finland as part of its Global Series in 2022 and 2024 and hasn't confirmed any future games there yet.

As of the opening day of the 2026-27 season in September, there were 53 Russians on NHL rosters, making up 7.3% of the league. That was the fourth-largest contingent of players from any country.

Russian wing Andrei Svechnikov had an assist for the Hurricanes in Thursday's 4-1 win over the Kraken in Helsinki. Pyotr Kochetkov was Carolina's backup goaltender. The Hurricanes and Kraken play again in Finland on Saturday.

The government decisions Thursday followed a backlash in Finland to Russia being reinstated for the ice hockey world championships, but its effects could mostly be felt in other sports. The International Skating Union warned of a "possible consequential impact" on its figure skating world championships in Finland in March.

Public broadcaster ERR reported Friday that Estonia had written to the International Ski and Snowboard Federation that athletes from Russia and its ally Belarus would not be allowed to enter the country. Estonia hosts the world junior championships in Nordic skiing in January.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's Week 10 lineup advice
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone delivers his lineup advice for Week 10.
articles.body:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 10 rankings .

Shough has been fairly predictable through the Saints' first eight games this season. In the four games where he's played defenses in the top half of the league for most points allowed to quarterbacks, Shough has finished as a top-eight fantasy QB each time. However, in the other four contests against stronger defenses, he's been the QB15 or worse.

While the Panthers are technically giving up the 13th-fewest fantasy points to passers this year, those numbers are misleading when you factor in the injuries to starters like Jaycee Horn and Bobby Okereke. The Saints offense is also getting healthier after the returns of first-round rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. last week.

The most intriguing aspect of this contest is the potential volume. Both teams rank inside the top seven in neutral pace of play this season and the game has a very solid projected point total of 49.5. That has Shough firmly inside my top-10 at the position this week.

Patrick Mahomes at Falcons – While it might take Josh Downs some time to learn the offense in Kansas City, his presence is a boost for the Chiefs' passing attack. Mahomes has multiple touchdown passes in six of his eight outings this year. Now, he gets a Falcons defense that's permitted three top-10 QB results, including Joe Burrow's four-touchdown effort last Sunday.

Bryce Young at Saints – Young benefitted from an easier schedule in the early part of the season, before struggling in some tougher matchups. Fortunately, he's coming off a quality performance versus a tough Broncos defense. That bodes well for him in what projects to be an uptempo game against the Saints, who are allowing the 12th-most fantasy points to QBs.

Malik Willis heading to injured reserve is a concerning development for a young Dolphins offense that had been showing promise in recent weeks. While his absence will be a serious problem in tougher matchups, it shouldn't derail Gordon this week against his easiest opponent yet.

The Colts are the fourth-most generous defense to fantasy running backs and are heading in the wrong direction over the last couple of weeks after trading away defensive stalwart DeForest Buckner. Indy has been hit hard by Bhayshul Tuten (159 yards, two TDs), Chris Rodriguez Jr. (58 yards, TD), Javonte Williams (124 yards, TD) and Tyler Goodson (77 yards) over the past two games alone.

Gordon continues to be productive, even in more difficult matchups, but this is a spot for a spike week as the offense leans on him with Kyle McCord under center.

Jonathan Taylor vs. Dolphins – Despite a brief decline in playing time the last couple of weeks while rumors swirled about a potential trade, Taylor remained with Indy. With the Colts being favored by four points, I'm expecting to see his touches rise against the Dolphins. Miami is also allowing the eighth-most fantasy points to RBs, including double-digit fantasy points to at least one running back each week.

Breece Hall vs. Bills – In his first game back from injury, Hall played fewer snaps than backup Braelon Allen, but dominated volume with 19 touches for 87 scrimmage yards against the Chiefs' tough run defense. That's a much tougher draw than this week's opponent, the Bills, who are the 10th-easiest defense for fantasy RBs in 2026.

Zach Charbonnet at Raiders – Charbonnet assumed the lead back role in his second game since returning from a torn ACL, playing 56% of the snaps and turning 17 touches into 86 yards versus the Cardinals. Next up is a Raiders defense that's been a springboard for fantasy RBs, allowing the third most points to the position, including seven top-12 weekly results in nine outings.

If you can't tell, I'm targeting the Saints-Panthers game pretty heavily for fantasy.

McMillan has been solid but not spectacular this season, especially when the matchups have been more challenging. He's failed to top 60 yards in any of the past three games against the Bucs, Packers and Broncos, but thankfully a touchdown saved his fantasy day in Week 9.

Though the Saints aren't exactly a pushover this week, they have let six different receivers post double-digit points in the past five outings. That includes both Browns wideouts hitting the mark last Sunday with KC Concepcion amassing 85 yards and a touchdown, while Denzel Boston poured in 98 yards.

This is a spot to confidently play both McMillan and Jalen Coker as fantasy WR2s.

Zay Flowers vs. Chargers – The arrival of Jacoby Brissett breathes life back into Flowers' fantasy outlook. While it might take some time for their connection to form, Flowers should be productive this week against a Chargers defense that's the fifth-softest matchup for receivers and allowed five touchdowns to the Texans' wideouts in Week 9.

Rashee Rice at Falcons – For all the flak sent in Rice's direction this season, he's managed to produce against a difficult schedule. All five of his appearances have come against defenses in the top-12 for fewest fantasy points allowed to his position, but he's still averaging WR24 stats on a per game basis. The Falcons are actually the most generous defense he's faced on paper, giving up the 13th-most points to WRs.

DJ Moore at Jets – In his three healthy games before last week, Moore had posted 100 yards and a TD versus the Texans, 67 yards against the Chargers, as well as 82 yards and a TD against the Ravens. Don't let a down game in a matchup with a fierce Vikings defense scare you away. Moore is a fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside most weeks.

With Josh Downs and Keenan Allen traded away, Tyler Warren is the only proven pass-catcher remaining in the Colts offense. He's currently averaging the fourth-most targets among tight ends, but he'll challenge for the league lead in that category the rest of the way.

The only question is whether he can capitalize on the volume in a struggling Colts offense. While the added defensive attention will be a problem in tougher matchups, I'm not as concerned about it this week.

The Dolphins are the fourth-easiest opponent for fantasy tight ends and the Colts are somehow favored in this game. That means you can start Warren as a top-five option at the position.

Darren Waller at Saints – Waller is a boom-or-bust fantasy TE2, who's coming off his biggest boom of the year with eight catches, 90 yards and a touchdown on 10 targets against the Broncos. The Saints are another favorable opponent, allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to TEs.

Tyler Higbee at Cardinals – Higbee had a three-game streak with over 60 yards in each outing, before failing to reach 25 yards in any of his past four appearances. However, with Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson sidelined, Higbee is back in the mix as a volume-based TE2 streamer.

Jonathan Gannon has the Packers defense playing extremely well and that's been without Micah Parsons, who is nearing a return in the coming weeks. Green Bay has held six of the last eight quarterbacks it's encountered to one touchdown or less.

The excitement around Cousins' return to Minnesota is well deserved and will result in some fantastic fantasy performances between now and the end of the season. But I'm taking a cautious approach in his first start since the trade.

Cousins projects as a risky QB2 versus the Packers and there are simply better streaming options available at the position.

Matthew Stafford at Cardinals – Stafford hasn't thrown for more than 228 yards in any game over the last month and has been held to just a single touchdown in each of his past two contests. Now, he'll try to get by without Puka Nacua. Even in a good matchup, it's hard to trust Stafford given his current weapons.

Fernando Mendoza vs. Seahawks – While I'm optimistic that Klint Kubiak can get the most out of Mendoza over the final two months, this isn't the game for fantasy managers to start the rookie. Seattle is the second-worst matchup for fantasy QBs.

Judkins has only played 39% and 34% of the snaps during his last two games, which coincides with the return of backup Dylan Sampson.

We might want to put backup in quotes since Sampson has out-snapped (96-52) and out-gained (117-94) Judkins during that span, with Judkins being held under 50 scrimmage yards in both contests and not finding the end zone.

To make matters worse, Sampson has the bigger role as a pass-catcher, limiting Judkins' fantasy outlook even more. The Texans aren't a bad matchup, but if Judkins didn't come through in an ideal setup against the Saints last week, I don't have much faith in him delivering here.

Consider this backfield a 50-50 split with Judkins being more of a TD-or-bust fantasy RB3 moving forward.

Tyler Allgeier vs. Rams – With Bam Knight expected to return this week, Allgeier won't dominate work the way he did in Week 9. Arizona will also be dealing with a Rams defense that's allowing the fourth-fewest fantasy points to RBs.

Kaleb Johnson vs. Vikings – Johnson will likely lead the Packers' backfield with Josh Jacobs sidelined, but unfortunately the next three weeks involve bad matchups with the Vikings and Rams, sandwiched around a bye. He's a TD-or-bust flex option due to a limited receiving role.

Omarion Hampton at Ravens – Hampton is still in a three-way committee and hasn't topped 60 scrimmage yards in six games. He's another TD-or-bust flex option.

Metcalf is preparing for another battle with DJ Turner and the Bengals defense. We know Metcalf is the kind of streaky receiver who can erupt in any contest, but he's been held to 50 yards or less in each of his last three meetings with Cincinnati.

That includes a three-catch, 31-yard outing against them in Week 3, which he salvaged with a touchdown.

The outlook is similar here, with Metcalf being a risky fantasy WR3 who will likely need a TD to come through for his managers.

Tre Tucker vs. Seahawks – Tucker had three spike-weeks this season, but has been held under 60 yards in every other game. This isn't the week to chase a big performance against the Seahawks defense that's allowing the fewest fantasy points to WRs.

Keenan Allen at Cowboys – After being traded to San Francisco, Allen is suiting up against the Cowboys for the second straight week. As a member of the Colts, he only managed 26 yards on four catches last Sunday. While he's the type of veteran receiver who could get up to speed quickly with his new club, it's very risky to trust him in his first game with a Niners team that has only had one WR top 40 yards in each of their last five contests.

Khalil Shakir at Jets – Shakir is a low-ceiling volume play who hasn't topped 25 yards in any of his last three games versus the Jets. He's an option if you're in a bye-week pinch, but don't get your hopes up for a big game this week.

Strange has only seen two targets each of the last two weeks, as the Jags have been able to lean on their rushing attack en route to easy victories.

It seems logical we'll see more of the same with Jacksonville entering this game as 10.5-point favorites over the Titans.

That makes Strange a low-volume fantasy TE2, who will likely need to score a touchdown before things get out of hand.

Mike Gesicki vs. Steelers – Six touchdowns in eight games has been impressive, but Gesicki is threading a very thin needle with 11 yards or less in three of his last four outings. He's just a TD-or-bust TE2 against Pittsburgh.

Mark Andrews vs. Chargers – While the arrival of Jacoby Brissett is good news for the Ravens' passing attack, it doesn't change the outlook for Andrews. The veteran hasn't eclipsed 30 yards in five straight games. His playing time is also on the decline, at under 60% of the snaps the last three weeks.

articles.title: Gemma y Delfi se la pegan y reabren la pelea por el número uno
articles.standfirst: Las líderes del ranking cayeron en cuartos de final del P1 de Dubái por primera vez esta temporada
articles.summary: Las líderes del ranking cayeron en cuartos de final del P1 de Dubái por primera vez esta temporada
articles.body: Parecía todo visto para sentencia en el pádel femenino tras la consecución del Major de Kuwait por parte de Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea. Sin embargo, en el P1 de Dubái se ha reabierto la pelea debido a un tropiezo de las número uno en cuartos de final ante Tamara Icardo y Claudia Jensen. Una derrota inesperada que vuelve a apretar todo en la zona alta del ranking. Se medían las número uno a una de las duplas más complicadas en estas instancias. Después de dar un golpe encima de la mesa en Kuwait, Triay y Brea llegaban a la ciudad emiratí con opciones de cerrar de manera casi definitiva su liderato un año más. No obstante, Jensen e Icardo tenían otros planes, dándole más emoción al circuito femenino, que podría decidirse en el Tour Finals de Barcelona. En el primer partido de la jornada, Claudia y Tamara arrancaron mejor, ganando el primer set y encendiendo todas las alarmas. La reacción no tardó en llegar y el 6-3 inicial se igualó con otro 6-3 que lo mandaba todo al tercero. Ahí llegó la debacle que nadie se esperaba: saltó la sorpresa en la pista central con un 6-1 que eliminaba a las pupilas de Seba Nerone. Tenían que aprovechar la oportunidad Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero, las inmediatas perseguidoras y principales candidatas a asaltar el trono. El tropiezo de la menorquina y la argentina ponía la presión sobre la dupla catalana, que no falló. Firmaron un partido muy sólido ante Jimena Velasco y Raquel Eugenio que se resolvió con un 6-2 y 6-3. Lanzadas hasta las semifinales, mantienen el objetivo de levantar el título, sumar 1.000 puntos e intentar seguir recortando distancias en México. Se enfrentarán a Paula Josemaría y Bea González. Otro clásico que se repite y que nuevamente decidirá parte de la lucha por el número uno. La ‘Perla’ y ‘Dinamita’ sacaron adelante su cruce de cuartos de final ante Marina Guinart y Ale Alonso por 6-1 y 6-3, convirtiéndose en el último obstáculo antes de la pelea por el título. Por el otro lado del cuadro, Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo siguen intratables. Como un rodillo vuelven a ganar y se medirán precisamente ante Jensen e Icardo, aunque tuvieron que trabajar una sufrida victoria contra Lorena Rufo y Victoria Iglesias por 7-6 y 6-4.

articles.title: Wisconsin freshman Ryan Hopkins could help Badgers finally stabilize their quarterback situation
articles.summary: (AP) — Ryan Hopkins never backed down from his decision to play at Wisconsin, even as the Badgers went through a revolving door of quarterbacks while having...
articles.body:
MADISON, Wis. (AP) — Ryan Hopkins never backed down from his decision to play at Wisconsin, even as the Badgers went through a revolving door of quarterbacks while having one of the nation's lowest-ranked offenses his senior year of high school.

"I just saw what it could be," Hopkins said. "I saw the future of this program."

That future has arrived midway through Hopkins' freshman season.

Hopkins made his first start last week and went 18 of 24 for 241 yards with three touchdown passes in a 31-10 victory over Rutgers. That performance earned Hopkins another start Saturday at Maryland (3-6, 1-5 Big Ten), raising hopes that the Badgers (6-3, 4-2) finally have found a long-term fix for one of their biggest issues.

Wisconsin's had nine different quarterbacks start games over the last four seasons. Hopkins is only the second of those quarterbacks who signed with Wisconsin directly out of high school rather than transferring there.

He committed to Wisconsin in the spring of 2025 and stuck with the Badgers as they went 4-8 last season. Hopkins had faith in coach Luke Fickell's staff and believed he could help make it work here.

"I think Ryan just wanted to be a part of a program's revival, to bring something great back to Wisconsin," said Hopkins' father, David Hopkins.

Hopkins grew up as the youngest sibling in a family full of athletes.

His sister Haley plays professional soccer for the KC Current. Holly Hopkins plays beach volleyball for College of Charleston. Another sister, Hannah, competed in track in college and rowed.

They competed with their little brother in everything from soccer to dodgeball when he was still a little kid who wasn't old enough to beat them consistently.

"All they wanted to do was get to him, get under his skin by beating him," David Hopkins recalled. "They know also as he grew up this wasn't going to work for them anymore. They had this sweet spot — a certain number of young years where they could toughen him up and humble him and make it known that you've got to earn it, buddy."

"I owe a lot to my family, the way I was raised," Ryan Hopkins said. "With my parents and my sisters, it was a competitive household. Obviously I get a lot of my competitive nature from that."

That background also helped bring Hopkins to Madison.

Hopkins says he enjoys being in a true college town. His father remembered enjoying road trips to face the Midwest League's Madison Muskies during his years playing minor league baseball in the Texas Rangers' system. Hopkins' mother, Beth Hopkins, noted the benefits of playing college football up north.

"If your ultimate goal is the NFL, you need to play in some weather," Beth Hopkins said. "That's the Midwest. That's the true, original Big Ten. If you get drafted by the Browns or Eagles and you've never played in the snow before, forget it."

Hopkins played soccer and baseball before devoting himself to football and becoming a quarterback. Teammates say that baseball background is apparent from the velocity of his passes.

"He throws like a pitcher," tight end Jacob Harris said. "It looks like he's going to through a missile through your chest, every single time he throws the ball."

High school transfer aided his development

Harris also noted the work ethic and confidence that have enabled Hopkins to set himself apart from the typical freshman. Hopkins prepared himself by transferring from JSerra Catholic in San Juan Capistrano, California, to spend his senior year at Mater Dei in Santa Ana.

It wasn't an easy choice. Beth Hopkins noted that her son was "pretty distraught about leaving his friends and coaches" at his old school. They put together a list of pros and cons before finally deciding to make the move to one of the nation's top high school programs.

Hopkins' pass catchers at Mater Dei included Ohio State's Chris Henry Jr. and Southern California teammates Kayden Dixon-Wyatt and Mark Bowman as well as Gavin Honore, who has committed to Oregon State.

"The competition you're surrounded by and the players you're with, the defense you're going against in practice every day, the defense you're going against on Friday nights, that just really helped me prepare at a high level," Hopkins said. "Obviously it's not the same as a college level … but the transition was a lot smoother."

His teammates notice the difference it's made in him.

"He's fearless," Harris said. "He's not going to flinch at anything. He's going to make decisions and live with them. Having a young guy, especially at that position, be so sure of himself so early is definitely something that's not exactly super common. I've certainly never seen it."

articles.title: Warriors superstar has wild rehab plan — and says he’ll fistfight GM to make it happen
articles.summary: Both members of the Golden State Warriors’ superstar backcourt duo are injured. Steph Curry is expected to miss at least several weeks after suffering an obl...
articles.body:
Both members of the Golden State Warriors' superstar backcourt duo are injured.

Steph Curry is expected to miss at least several weeks after suffering an oblique abdominal tear during Wednesday's game.

Jimmy Butler continues to work his way back to the court after tearing his ACL last season, and should be able to play in January or February.

When Butler is able to return, Golden State will have to choose whether they want him to play rehab games with their G League affiliate, the Santa Cruz Warriors, or return straight to Golden State.

Although Butler seems to have already made his decision.

"I'm going down to Santa Cruz to hoop. It may not be for long, but I'm going to play in Santa Cruz. I'm playing in a f****** game," Butler told The Athletic.

"I'm definitely coming down there to play. So good luck to everybody. Y'all ain't gonna get too many minutes out of me, but I'm definitely going down there. I want to hoop," he added.

Butler was then asked whether he got his desire to play in Santa Cruz cleared with Mike Dunleavy Jr., the Warriors' GM .

"I don't got to clear s*** with nobody. I'm going. Me and Mike will fistfight. He's gonna be like, 'Jimmy, no.' I'm gonna be like, 'Mike, yes. I'm going to G League, baby!' Y'all know where to find me. Santa Cruz, baby," Butler responded.

Butler was clearly just kidding. Plus, he and Dunleavy Jr. were teammates on the Chicago Bulls for three seasons, so they don't have a typical player-front office executive relationship.

Threat of violence aside, Dunleavy Jr. will probably appreciate how eager Butler is to return.

articles.title: In Disappointing and Injury-Riddled Season, Shohei Ohtani Finishes Second to Pete Crow-Armstrong in MVP Race
articles.summary: Los Ángeles Dodgers' four-time Most Valuable Player Shohei Ohtani did not win a fifth award. Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow Armstrong did, and deserve...
articles.body:
Los Ángeles Dodgers' four-time Most Valuable Player Shohei Ohtani did not win a fifth award. Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow Armstrong did , and deservedly so. Ohtani, who has two trophies from each league, finished in second place. It is the first time in four years that the baseball unicorn has not won the award, but it wasn't for lack of effort. However, injuries played a huge part in his downfall. As a result, Armstrong filled the void and did an outstanding job, completing a 40/40 season.

The only player to have won more MVPs than Shohei Ohtani is Barry Bonds , who owns seven. For a while, it looked like Ohtani was making another run at history. At the end of June, Ohtani had close to 30 home runs and was hitting close to a .300 average. He was the threat that every pitcher dreads at the top of the lineup. But that wasn't all; he maintained a 2.00 Earned Run Average as a starter in the Los Angeles rotation and was near the top of the league in inducing strikeouts. There hasn't been a two-way player with that resume since Babe Ruth.

It all fell apart at the beginning of July, when Ohtani was forced to opt out of the All-Star Game due to a sore knee. The injury persisted, and the consequences were most visible at the plate. After July 1, Ohtani barely stayed above a .200 batting average, driving in fewer than 20 runs, and only hit two home runs the rest of the season. It was obvious that he couldn't drive off his back leg.

Moreover, Ohtani was swinging at fastballs he usually drives over 400 feet, and nearly every swing drew a shake of the arm or a wince of pain. In short, Ohtani was a shell of himself, even after a stint on the 15-day Injured List. Thus, winning awards. or, for that matter, a World Series was out of the question.

The loss of a chance at a fifth MVP should be a cautionary tale for both Ohtani and the Dodgers. The lack of communication regarding the condition of the superstar's health is troubling. The insistence on throwing bullpen sessions after the knee issue popped up is downright baffling, particularly because both parties admitted that it was the act of throwing on the mound that caused the injury in the first place. It not only cost Ohtani the MVP but may have cost the Dodgers a chance at a three-peat as well. Going forward, discretion should be the better part of valor, even if the upcoming season appears to be abbreviated.

Ohtani has already etched his name among the greatest players ever to grace the baseball diamond. But going forward, the Dodgers have to make a better effort to preserve the health of their superstar so that he can keep pursuing not only prestigious individual awards but more World Series rings. They have already seen the consequences i f they don't put limitations on their Superman; he serves as his own Kryptonite. It doesn't help his team either. President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman has said that "surgery is not on the table" for Baseball's unicorn. That's good news. However, the Dodgers are left to wonder what could have been, had Ohtani been more open about his physical well-being.

Andrew Friedman said surgery is "not on the table" for Shohei Ohtani.

Said it was "whack a mole" between the knee, then the biceps throughout the year.

Friedman: "I fully expect him to pitch next year."

Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) October 21, 2026

Crow-Armstrong deserves the MVP Award. He had an outstanding year, and his 40/40 season put the rest of the league on notice of what one can do when healthy. The earlier Ohtani learns that, the better it is for him…and the Dodgers.

articles.title: 'If conditions are flat, watch out': Mike Hesson finds a bizarre way to defend Babar Azam's struggles in Pakistan team
articles.summary: While his struggles on the field continue, Pakistan Test skipper Babar Azam is defended bizarrely by head coach Mike Hesson, who praises the batter's ability...
articles.body:
Mike Hesson says Pakistan batter Babar Azam's problems are being exaggerated and blames the conditions.

Babar made 50 and 34 in the drawn first Test against Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi.

He has now gone 42 innings without a Test century.

Mike Hesson defends Babar Azam after Rawalpindi Test questions

Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has pushed back at the criticism of Babar Azam, arguing that his captain's scores say more about the pitch than about his batting.

Hesson spoke after the first Test against Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi ended in a draw. He began by dismissing the value of Babar's first-innings fifty, then said the seam movement left any batter at risk.

"Look, sometimes, those are condition-dependent. So I don't think the fifty he got in the first innings was a high-quality fifty. And you know, when the ball seams like that, sometimes it's going to have your number on it," Hesson said in a clip posted on X .

Hesson then turned to the numbers and finished with a warning about what happens when Babar gets a flat pitch.

"You look at Babar; he averages over 50 in Test cricket this year. It's the highest average for anybody who has played more than 10 innings. So to think he's got an issue is, I think, often overhyped. And I think, as I said, if the conditions are flat and he gets himself in, look out."

How did Babar Azam perform in the first Test vs Sri Lanka?

Sri Lanka put Pakistan in to bat on a green surface on day one, and four batters reached fifty, two of them on debut. Tayyab Arif made 57 and Mohammad Taha 51, while Babar contributed the 50 his coach has now talked down. Saud Shakeel took it furthest with 93, and Pakistan declared 434 for 9.

Sri Lanka answered with 446, with centuries from Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis carrying them to a 12-run lead and leaving the match without a clear favorite. Pakistan began the final day 45 ahead and had to bat out the day rather than chase anything. The match ended in the draw everyone expected.

Babar made 34 in that second innings, hitting six fours and adding 50 with Shakeel before Milan Rathnayaka set a leg-side trap and had him caught at short square leg. Kamindu Mendis had dropped him on 22. Salman Agha fell to the same plan for 13, and Pakistan finished the weather-hit match on 284 for 8.

Babar's struggles are not limited to conditions

The average Hesson leans on does not match what Babar did on his last tour. He missed the opening Test in England through injury, returned at Lord's for scores of 8 and 6, then made 76 and 7 at Edgbaston to finish that series with 97 runs at 24.25.

The century drought is the bigger gap in the argument. Babar's last Test hundred came against New Zealand in Karachi in December 2022, and the wait now stands at 42 innings.

Nobody is claiming he cannot score; the complaint is that he keeps getting in and giving it away, which is exactly what 50 and 34 at Rawalpindi looked like.

Hesson is right that the pitch had something in it, but Rathnayaka dismissed Babar with a planned leg-side trap rather than a seaming delivery with his name on it.

Regardless, all batters are expected to perform well on flat pitches because they help the ball come nicely onto the bat. The true skill of a batter is to excel in pitches that are challenging too - so Hesson's argument is a bit confusing.

The second Test starts in Rawalpindi on November 17 after being moved from Lahore because of smog, and Babar can settle the argument himself.

articles.title: What I Want To See From Penn State Vs Minnesota
articles.summary: Keep it winning!
articles.body:
Penn State has built a streak of their own, having beaten Purdue soundly and survived at Washington. On paper, the worst is now behind them, and all that stands between the Lions and a "respectable, given where they were at" record is this game.

The "second half" problems have been widely documented, and, for all his faults, one thing Matt Campbell has already shown is that it will consider addressing issues within reason. He said as much in his press conference this week, noting that the decision to not go for the jugular at the end of the first half against Washington is something to think about if they're in that same situation again (reasoning at the time being that momentum was on their side, and they didn't want to give it up. In other words, conservative).

If Penn State finds itself up big on Minnesota, with the ball, and the ability to make the game truly out of reach, I want the game to be truly out of reach.

articles.title: Four games that matter for Oregon's Big Ten title chances in Week 11
articles.summary: Oregon has slim hopes of making the Big Ten title game, with four games in particular affecting their chances in Week 11.
articles.body:
Having suffered three losses before the calendar flipped to November, the Oregon Ducks find themselves scrapping and clawing to make the Big Ten championship game, hoping to give themselves a shot at the College Football Playoff. It's not an enviable spot to be in, as the Ducks need to receive some help in order to reach the conference title game — but it's the spot that Oregon has put itself in.

They've done their part in digging themselves out of a hole, winning two straight must-wins against Northwestern and Ohio State. The wins must continue in the final three regular-season games, home contests against Michigan and Washington and road date with Michigan State. If they don't go 3-0, nothing else matters and the Ducks will be packing their bags for a no-name bowl game in roughly a month.

If they don't get some help, and the CFP Committee doesn't deem them worthy of receiving an at-large bid to the 12-team field, that same result will occur. Help is very much needed, and Week 11 is the most important week of them all.

Last week, there were ten teams with two or fewer losses in Big Ten play. Now, after Minnesota and Northwestern loss, that number is down to eight. Oregon is joined by five other teams with exactly two conference losses and hoping to be joined by a sixth after Week 11. Tiebreakers will almost certainly come into the picture.

Before we get too far ahead of ourselves, let's break down the four games that matter towards Oregon's chances of making the Big Ten title game in Week 11, assuming the Ducks take care of business against the Wolverines .

Illinois Fighting Illini vs. No. 4 UCLA Bruins (Friday)

Why it matters: This one's simple: UCLA wins and Illinois is essentially eliminated from the Big Ten title race with their third loss. The reason this matters for the Ducks is that the Fighting Illini hold the head-to-head tiebreaker after beating the Ducks in Champaign in October, Oregon's third loss of the year and second in conference. If Illinois miraculously wins on Friday night at the Rose Bowl over the undefeated Bruins, Duck fans should worry just a bit, but not too much. The Fighting Illini still have to play Iowa and Northwestern to finish the year. As long as they don't go undefeated, the Ducks will be fine. UCLA is basically a shoo-in as a representative in the Big Ten title game, so them winning on Friday doesn't mean anything for Oregon.

Where: SECU Stadium | | College Park, MD

Why it matters: Wisconsin is another squad with two conference losses, and the tiebreaker scenario could get quite complicated. Assuming Oregon wins out, the Ducks and Badgers have the same 2-1 record against common conference opponents. From there, it'd go to the record against the highest-finishing conference opponent, but both teams would've beaten the same common opponents (USC and Michigan State) and lost to the same opponent (UCLA). Then, the tiebreaker would go to the cumulative conference winning percentage of all conference opponents, something that won't be certain until the end of the regular season. To eliminate all of that potential confusion, an upset from the Terrapins would help the Ducks out tremendously.

No. 18 USC Trojans vs. No. 9 Indiana Hoosiers

Where: Memorial Stadium | | Bloomington, IN

Why it matters: This is the biggest one, and it's unfortunate that it's at the same time as Oregon's bout with Michigan. Duck fans, it might be worth rocking the two TV set-up if you're able to, as it holds a ton of weight in terms of the Ducks' Big Ten title chances. The Hoosiers are currently 5-1 in conference. If they win out, they face UCLA in the conference championship. But a loss to USC would knock them down to the two-loss crew and give Oregon the tie-breaker, as the Ducks would have a better record against common opponents thanks to their win over the Trojans. Oregon winning on Saturday is big, but arch-rival USC winning in Bloomington would put the Ducks in the driver's seat for the Big Ten title game. Just this week, Duck fans will have to root hard for the Trojans.

Where: Kinnick Stadium | | Iowa City, IA

Why it matters: Iowa is in a similar spot as Wisconsin, holding two conference losses with a relatively light remaining schedule of Purdue, Illinois and Nebraska remaining. With the same record against common opponents, the tie-breaker with Oregon (assuming both the Ducks and Hawkeyes win out) would go to the record against the highest common opponent in the standings. That's likely to be Ohio State, a team that Oregon beat and Iowa lost to. But if the Buckeyes crumble down the stretch, that could change and put the Ducks in jeopardy of losing a tie-breaker to Iowa. This would be another miraculous upset, but Purdue getting a win at Kinnick Stadium would further clear the path for Oregon.

articles.title: Reading missing key players for Stockport game
articles.summary: Reading head coach Leam Richardson will be without key players for their game against Stockport County on Saturday.
articles.body:
Reading head coach Leam Richardson has said he will be without a number of key players for their game against Stockport County on Saturday.

The Royals will miss some players because of injury, suspension and international call-ups as they travel away to take on the second-placed Hatters.

Richardson's team sit sixth in League One with six wins from 14 games.

They beat Peterborough United 5-0 in the FA Cup on Saturday before losing on penalties to Bristol Rovers on Tuesday in the Jersey Mike's Trophy.

"[Jacob] Brown is still struggling with his ribs coming off the back of Wednesday [against Oxford]," Richardson told BBC Radio Berkshire.

"Jeriel [Dorsett] has been called up to Montserrat but he's had a little knock as well so we'll be without the pair of them at the weekend.

"Paudie [O'Connor] is at five [yellow cards] so that'll be him suspended as well - it's a huge [miss] as he's been really consistent and reliable for us.

"He's a big personality on the pitch and off the pitch so it's disappointing because I didn't think it was a booking as well on Wednesday night in the Oxford game, but is what it is.

"We've got to make sure we overcome, adapt and make sure we prepare as well as possible for these games."

Reading will also be without injured defender Josh Knight and midfielder Andy Rinomhota, who Richardson believes will serve his suspension for picking up five yellow cards while on international duty with Zimbabwe.

Reading's match at Stockport on Saturday will be their fifth consecutive away game across all competitions, last playing at Select Car Leasing Stadium in late October.

Richardson said the club have had to carefully plan their travel and recovery in recent weeks as they played at Plymouth, Oxford, Peterborough, Bristol and now in Greater Manchester this weekend.

"We've had to make sure we're diligent with our travelling and everything else with our preparation," he added.

"I'm really looking forward to it and think it'd be a really good game. Fingers crossed we're prepared and get a positive result to finish these away days in this block off.

"They've been in the play-offs and have been recruiting very well, spending money on different players and always challenged at the top end of this level which is what every club is after.

"They're a really good team as well and are well-coached so it'll be a really good game."

articles.title: 'It was actually a self-own': ESPN reporter has unique theory on 24-team CFP
articles.summary: As more information comes out about the expansion of the College Football Playoff to 24 teams, one thing is certain: Almost nobody wanted this. Just this wee...
articles.body:
As more information comes out about the expansion of the College Football Playoff to 24 teams, one thing is certain: Almost nobody wanted this.

Just this week, The Athletic reported that even ESPN, which has broadcast rights to the entire tournament, didn't support the idea . And a Nielsen survey showed that 90 percent of respondents who considered themselves college football fans also didn't support it—which CFP executive director Rich Clark acknowledged ( and ignored) this week.

Yet here we are, with the first 24-team bracket set to arrive next winter . And ESPN's Dan Wetzel believes that by chasing "credibility" with the weekly rankings show, the committee dug a grave for its own credibility and forced itself to expand to please critics.

"One of the reasons we expanded this Playoff is by doing these weekly rankings over the years. They absolutely killed the credibility of the committee," Wetzel said Wednesday on The College GameDay Podcast .

"And so every week, these things come out, it's literally a half-baked pie, and then you let everybody tee off on you. And so it is either, in the media, people who are going to get far more engagement on the outrage algorithm of saying, 'This is the dumbest committee of all time,' they did this, or they did that. Or, these coaches who sit around and complain about, 'We're just not getting respect because we're not this or we're not that.'"

By opening up its deliberations to scrutiny, the committee ultimately may have revealed its own shortcomings. Beyond the complaints that Wetzel highlights, even genuine analysis of the rankings each week would underscore faulty arguments. The week-to-week selection of teams that qualify for the postseason is far less exact than a big, fancy rankings show makes it out to be.

And Wetzel believes that the committee was so sensitive to the criticism it faced that it inevitably embraced arguments from teams and conferences that used these inexact rankings cases to argue that, in fact, more teams were worthy of a Playoff berth.

" There's an entire economy on ripping the hell out of the committee , which undermines the value of the committee and undermines that this Playoff isn't successful, and hence we need to expand the Playoff," Wetzel explained.

"It was not an organized activity. It was actually a self-own by the Playoff people who wanted this to work. But you can draw a pretty quick line between deciding we're going to put out a half-baked ranking and why we went from a four-team Playoff to a 24-team Playoff in four short years. And part of it is they just allowed this to be smashed up, and it's like, who the hell cares where they're ranked right now? We'll find out."

The committee doesn't seem to agree. The rankings will continue even under the 24-team format, though host Rece Davis acknowledged they need to be " reimagined " so as not to bore the audience with a long list of mediocre teams in the lower seeds.

But in its quest to spark conversation and be "accountable" in its process, the CFP may have put itself in a doom spiral that led to a result nobody truly asked for.

articles.title: Timberwolves’ Practices Lift LaMelo Ball to New Playmaking Heights
articles.summary: All it took was two Minnesota Timberwolves practices to make LaMelo Ball look like the floor general the team hoped they were getting when they traded for Ba...
articles.body:
All it took was two Minnesota Timberwolves practices to make LaMelo Ball look like the floor general the team hoped they were getting when they traded for Ball this summer .

The timing of the practices was key — rare back-to-back sessions the team was able to conduct because they had three days off in the middle of a Timberwolves' record eight-game homestand . For the first time since Anthony Edwards ' surgery, the team had a chance to step back, take a breath, and work on how they want to play in Edwards' absence .

Assistant coach Paolo Prigioni told the media that the Wolves "really took advantage of these two days" of practice, and it showed, particularly in Ball's play Thursday. He finished with 22 points and a season-high nine assists as the Wolves throttled a good Dallas team 133-94.

LaMelo Ball Controlled the Game From the Opening Tip

On the Mavericks' first possession, 15 seconds after the opening tip, Ball found Jonathan Kuminga for a layup on a textbook pick-and-roll. Whether that was a set play from the Timberwolves' practices or not, it seemed to get Ball going.

In the next two minutes, Ball found Kuminga and Jaden McDaniels for dunks, then hit a three-pointer. He finished with six threes on the night, but this game was more about his playmaking than his shotmaking.

Ball has had big scoring nights in his 12 games with Minnesota, including a 34-point performance in a Nov. 2 win over Milwaukee. But he had never had more than eight assists before Thursday. Against Dallas, he had eight in the first half and finished with nine despite sitting most of the second half and playing just 25 minutes total.

Ball didn't need those two Timberwolves' practices to improve as a scorer — he gets plenty of shots up on his own time. He needed the Timberwolves' practices to improve his chemistry and connection with his teammates, and step up as a playmaker in the wake of Edwards' injury .

The Ball-Gobert Connection Showed Signs of Life

Ball also showed an improved connection with Rudy Gobert on Thursday, a development that's incredibly important to the Timberwolves moving forward. One of the team's aspirations in acquiring Ball was to unlock the 7-foot-1 Gobert as a lob threat like he was in Utah.

The early returns on that have not been great. The timing between Ball and Gobert has looked off, and the combination of Ball's penchant for quick, no-look passes and Gobert's iffy hands has led to many balls sailing out of bounds.

There was one of those Thursday, as Ball fired a pass that went right between Gobert's big mitts early in the game. But after that, Ball and Gobert connected on two lobs — one that Gobert dunked emphatically with two hands and another that he laid in softly.

Improving those lobs was likely a focus in the Timberwolves' practices because, with Edwards out, they need more scoring from Gobert. He finished with just nine points on Thursday, but, like Ball, he played limited minutes in the blowout win. On a per-minute basis, his production was encouraging.

The way Ball got everyone going against Dallas was contagious, and six Timberwolves scored in double figures. They had 33 assists on 52 made baskets as a team and shot 58% from the field. By almost every metric, it was their top offensive performance of the season.

Videos of practices have shown the Timberwolves' chemistry , including a recent one in which Edwards cut up with his teammates despite being on crutches . Having a couple of days to get together and work on things seems to have only made this 9-3 team better and solidified Ball's place as the team's offensive leader with Ant out.

articles.title: Three call-ups, three goals: This is what Devils depth looks like
articles.summary: The Devils' callups immediately contributed on Thursday.
articles.body:
Three players came up from Utica. All three scored. One tied the game, one won it and one gave the Devils enough breathing room to exhale.

That's a pretty good night for the guys who weren't in the lineup the last time the Devils played.

Lenni Hämeenaho, Vladislav Kolyachonok and Stefan Noesen all scored in Thursday's 5–2 win over the Capitals at Prudential Center. Connor Hellebuyck made 26 saves to improve to 6-0-0, a franchise record.

For Saturday's rematch between the Devils and the Capitals, the over/under is set at 6.5 total goals on Kalshi . Also, view our in-depth guide to the best sportsbook promos to shop for the most competitive odds.

Brenden Dillon played what Sheldon Keefe thought might have been his best game of the season, and the Devils did all of it on a night when their coach flat-out said they weren't at their best.

That's the part that should get your attention. The schedule has been a grind, bodies are coming out of the lineup and the Devils are still finding different guys to win them hockey games.

Hämeenaho got the first one. The Devils were down 2–1 in the second when Dillon put a puck toward the net and it went in off Hämeenaho's glove. He showed the mark it left in the locker room afterward.

"It wasn't a pretty one, but I'll take that every day of the week," Hämeenaho said.

Then came Kolyachonok, playing his third game in three nights and his first as a Devil. By the third period, he'd put a puck on net from the blue line that found its way in for the winner.

And then Noesen looked like he got shot out of a cannon. He raced to a loose puck and roofed a backhander to make it 4–2. Jack Hughes added the empty-netter.

General manager Sunny Mehta has been preaching depth since he got to New Jersey. "Optionality" is a big deal to him at every level of the organization, and this is what it looks like.

Brenden Dillon needs to be in the lineup

Dillon had been sitting. With Brett Pesce and Johnathan Kovacevic unavailable on Thursday, the Devils needed him to do more than just take a regular shift. He helped create the tying goal, and Kolyachonok said the two talked before the game to make sure they were on the same page.

"I thought in lots of ways, Dilly had his best game of the season here tonight," Keefe said. "He's just competing hard, and he's a very proud guy."

Dillon finished the game with an assist, a plus-two rating, two shots, two blocks, and four hits in 18:31.

Keefe praised Dillon's "character, leadership, presence, perspective," and talked about the relationships he has with everyone from the younger players to the guys who've been here for years.

Dillon is a throwback. There's a place for a defenseman who competes like that, can help get a guy through his first game with the team and still gets a puck through when the Devils need a goal. Thursday was a reminder of why he should be playing every night.

Six starts, six wins for Connor Hellebuyck

Hellebuyck became the first goalie in franchise history to win his first six starts with the Devils. Remember all the noise about him sitting in Winnipeg? The Devils put him back in net for a division game and took two points in regulation.

The record is the headline. What he changes for the skaters in front of him might be the bigger deal. Evan Rodrigues explained that the defensemen feel more comfortable stepping up to keep plays alive because if there's a bad bounce, Hellebuyck is there to bail them out. Pair that with forwards tracking back and suddenly the Devils can spend more time keeping a team pinned in its own end.

They still have things to fix. Rodrigues scored on the second power-play unit, but the penalty kill gave one back. Keefe said the Devils weren't at their best and didn't know if they'd be there Saturday, either.

articles.title: Hutton among trio to sign new Notts deals
articles.summary: Nottinghamshire seam bowler Brett Hutton is among a trio of players to sign new deals with the County Championship side.
articles.body:
Nottinghamshire seam bowler Brett Hutton is among a trio of players to sign new deals with the County Championship side.

The 33-year-old, who was the club's leading wicket-taker with 38 when they won the Division One title in 2025, has agreed to remain at Trent Bridge until the end of the 2028 campaign.

Hutton has spent 13 seasons with Nottinghamshire across two spells and has taken 357 wickets across all formats for them.

Fellow seam bowler Tom Giles, 20, and 23-year-old all-rounder Ben Martindale have also extended their stays with the club, having both come though the academy as Hutton did more than a decade earlier.

"I always want to keep making a difference for us in every facet of the game, and having been around the club for a while now, I also want to help the younger players coming through," Hutton told the club's website.

"I've got the same hunger to perform and help this team achieve success that I've always had, and there's a great feeling among the strong group that we've got here at the moment."

Giles, who has signed a new two-year deal, made his first-class debut for the club last season and went on to take five wickets in four County Championship appearances.

Martindale, whose father Duncan also played for Nottinghamshire, has featured 32 times across all formats and has been a regular in the club's second XI side for a number of years. His new deal keeps him at Trent Bridge for a further 12 months.

articles.title: Siena's league adding Stonehill College for 2027-28 season
articles.summary: Stonehill, located in Easton, Mass., is the second NEC school in three weeks to accept an invitation from the Metro. Le Moyne College in Syracuse is also joi...
articles.body:
The Metro Conference keeps getting bigger at the Northeast Conference's expense.

The Metro, which includes Siena University, announced Friday the addition of Stonehill College, effective July 1, 2027, to bring the league's membership to a record 14 schools for the 2027-28 season.

Stonehill, located in North Easton, Mass., is the second NEC school in three weeks to accept an invitation from the Metro. Le Moyne College in Syracuse is also joining the Metro in 2027-28 .

Mount St. Mary's, Merrimack and Sacred Heart have also departed the NEC for the Metro since 2022.

"We are excited to welcome Stonehill College as the 14th member of the Metro Conference," said Metro commissioner Travis Tellitocci said in a news release. "With an outstanding campus, the excitement surrounding the development of Bogan Arena, and a clear vision for the future, Stonehill has demonstrated a strong commitment to investing in its Division I athletics program and is an institution on the rise. Our Council of Presidents has been intentional in identifying institutions that are committed to investing in athletics and positioning themselves for long-term success."

Fairfield is leaving the Metro for the Coastal Athletic Association after this academic year.

Stonehill began its reclassification from Division II to Division I in July 22 and completed an accelerated transition on July 1, 2025. The Skyhawks became full NCAA Division I active members for the 2025-26 academic year.

Stonehill previously belonged to the Division II Northeast 10 Conference, where the Skyhawks were rivals of The College of Saint Rose, which closed in 2024.

Last May, Stonehill announced a planned $50 million improvement of its athletic facilties, including a new basketball and hockey arena. Stonehill said it had $22.5 million in commitments. Stonehill is a Division I independent in hockey.

Last season, Stonehill men's basketball went 12-21 and the women's team was 12-18. The teams currently play in Merkert Gymnasium, with a capacity of 1,560.

Siena president Chuck Seifert, who is chair of the Metro Council of Presidents, said "Stonehill embodies everything the Metro stands for" because of its academic excellence, strong faith-based values and commitment to investing in Division I athletics.

"At a time of significant shift throughout the NCAA, this move underscores our league's determination to be proactive and bold in shaping our own trajectory," Seifert said. "Reaching a record 14 member institutions and strengthening our New England footprint enhances our competitive landscape."

Frank Ambrose, who is Siena's advisor to athletic director John D'Argenio for revenue sharing and NIL strategy, was less enthusiastic about adding another team from the NEC, historically one of the lowest-rated conferences in Division I basketball.

Ambrose questioned how it would strengthen men's basketball and keep the Metro champion from needing to play in the NCAA Tournament's opening round, which will be played in Dayton, Ohio, and Wichita, Kan. with the tournament's expansion to 76 teams.

"I'm sorry I just don't see this as a net plus but the conference has been playing defense for years and our NET rating shows that," Ambrose posted on X. "Maybe @StonehillMBB will be a Merrimack add but what is the @MetroConfSports actual plan continuing to reach into the @NEC, locking us into a trip to Dayton???"

Mount St. Mary's men's basketball won the Metro championship in 2025. Merrimack won the regular-season title by three games last season before losing to Siena in the championship game in Atlantic City.

Siena has belonged to the Metro since the 1989-90 season. With Fairfield's departure, Iona, Manhattan and Saint Peter's are the remaining charter members from the league's first season in 1981-82.

articles.title: Estonia latest country to ban Russian athletes as backlash intensifies
articles.summary: Estonia is the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine.
articles.body:
Estonia has become the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine.

It comes after Norway, Finland and Canada made similar announcements.

The moves come amid a mounting backlash over the reinstatement of athletes from Russia and Belarus.

In September, the International Ski Federation (FIS) relaxed its rules, saying competitors from the two countries would be granted access to its events "provided that they sign a declaration of neutrality".

They had previously faced more stringent background checks on any voluntary link or paid duty with the military.

Participation remains limited to individual events, with athletes banned from displaying national symbols such as flags, anthems or uniforms.

However, it has now emerged that Estonia's government has written to the FIS, claiming that allowing entry to competitors from Russia and Belarus would undermine the country's support of Ukraine, and present an opportunity for propaganda.

In a statement issued to BBC Sport, the FIS said it "is committed to offering full support to athletes, national ski associations and local organisers - with most of which we have a long-standing relationship - in the process of navigating what we know to be a very complex situation.

"With that said, the Individual Neutral Athlete policy is clear in stating that notwithstanding eligibility, the host country visa and entry policies remain in place and are determined solely by the host country. FIS bears no responsibility for denial of visas or entry to any person granted eligibility under the FIS Individual Neutral Athlete Policy."

On Thursday, Scandinavian neighbours Norway and Finland both said they would also block visas for Russian athletes because of the war in Ukraine.

Norway is preparing to host the cross-country skiing World Cup next month, while Finland is due to stage the figure skating world championships in March. The International Skating Union (ISU) has said it "believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing", and that it was "seeking clarifications" from officials in Finland.

This comes in the wake of last month's decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to overturn a ban of Russia by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), a move condemned by the British, German, Finnish and Czech federations.

Russia have been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in February 2022, but the Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RIHF) then successfully appealed that decision at Cas. The court said that IIHF arguments citing safety and security were "not supported by sufficient evidence", but the Hockey Federation of Ukraine said the ruling caused "special outrage".

The Canadian government has since informed its hockey authorities that it will not issue visas for Russians to play in next month's World Junior Championship, including those who currently play for teams in Canada, as long as the war continues. A number of countries had said they would refuse to play against Russia, if they were allowed to take part.

Despite the controversy, the return of Russia and Belarus to international sport has been gathering pace this year.

In March, several athletes from the two countries were allowed to compete under their national flags at the Winter Paralympics after partial suspensions by the International Paralympic Committee were lifted.

In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally reinstated Russia to its competitions, stating a ban introduced in 2023 after the invasion of Ukraine was "no longer applicable".

However, sports federations can still enforce their own eligibility criteria. While World Gymnastics, World Aquatics and World Boxing have all removed restrictions on Russian athletes competing, a total ban has been maintained by World Athletics.

Last month, it was announced that Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
