articles.title: F1 Reporter Banned for Rest of Season by FIA After Criticism of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc
articles.summary: Formula 1 Racing's governing body has banned a reporter from covering races in person for the remainder of the 2026 season after they recently wrote an article criticizing driver Charles Leclerc.
articles.body:
Formula 1 Racing's governing body has banned a reporter from covering races in person for the remainder of the 2026 season after they recently wrote an article criticizing driver Charles Leclerc.

According to Dan Sheldon of The Athletic, Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile general manager Alberto Villarreal sent a letter to Daily Mail reporter Jonathan McEvoy, informing him of the FIA's decision.

"The FIA considers that your article falls short of the standards of professionalism expected of media representatives accredited to cover the FIA Formula 1 world championship," the letter read. "Accordingly, the FIA has decided to exercise its discretion under the 2026 FIA Formula 1 world championship accreditation guidelines to withdraw your media accreditation for the remainder of the 2026 season, with immediate effect."

As a result of the ban, McEvoy will not be given media credentials for the final three races of the season, which are the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Qatar Grand Prix and Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Per Sheldon, McEvoy wrote an opinion piece on Nov. 4 in which he called Leclerc a "sneaky little b-----d" following Leclerc's run-in with Lewis Hamilton during the Mexico Grand Prix.

Despite being Hamilton's teammate with Ferrari, Leclerc battled with Hamilton for the lead on the opening lap of the Mexico Grand Prix, resulting in both of them going off the track.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen went on to win the race, while Hamilton finished second and Leclerc came in fourth.

Hamilton suggested after the race that he and Leclerc were able to bury the hatchet, telling Sky Sports (h/t ESPN's Nate Saunders ), "Me and Charles, we sat and spoke and we squashed it and we're moving on. I think we still have a huge amount of respect for each other. I'm glad we had a chat and now we move on."

McEvoy wrote the column about Leclerc nonetheless, although he went on to say that his comments about Leclerc were "light-hearted" and "joshing" in nature, per Sheldon.

Daily Mail head of sport Chris Dean provided a statement to Sheldon in which he admonished the FIA for its decision, saying, "This is an unprecedented and outrageous attack on the freedom of the press. We are in dangerous territory when the FIA react in such a heavy-handed way to some mild and fair criticism of one driver."

While there are still three races remaining in the 2026 F1 season, the drivers' and constructors' champions have already been determined.

Kimi Antonelli, 20, clinched his first career F1 title at the Mexico Grand Prix on Nov. 1, and Mercedes clinched its ninth constructors' championship at the São Paulo Grand Prix on Nov. 8.

articles.title: Flyers Fan Calls for Rick Tocchet's Firing in Photo of Billboard Amid Matvei Michkov Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Philadelphia Flyers head coach Rick Tocchet is under fire, as a new billboard calling for his firing debuted on Friday.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Flyers head coach Rick Tocchet is under fire, as a new billboard calling for his firing debuted on Friday.

X user Tony Escargot posted a photo of the billboard, which appeals to Flyers general manager Daniel Brière and reads, "Danny. Fire Tocchet now."

According to Matt Schultz of CrossingBroad.com, the billboard debuted one day after a crowd-funded billboard that read, "Fire Tocchet. Save Michkov," went up in South Philadelphia.

Tocchet has drawn the ire of Flyers fans in the wake of a report by ESPN's Kevin Weekes this week in which he noted that Michkov "would likely want a new start elsewhere."

Selected seventh overall by the Flyers in the 2023 NHL draft, the 21-year-old Michkov is arguably the franchise's best player, as he leads the team with 10 goals and 15 points in 21 games this season.

Michkov is set to become a restricted free agent this offseason, and Weekes' report suggests he would prefer to get traded than to sign a new contract with the Flyers.

The Flyers were among the biggest surprises of the 2025-26 season, finishing with 98 points and beating the Pittsburgh Penguins in the first round of the playoffs before getting swept by the eventual Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes in the second.

That marked the first time the Flyers had made the playoffs since the 2019-20 campaign.

Tocchet was hired as the Flyers' new head coach prior to the 2025-26 season, and he seemed to change the culture, as Philly enjoyed a 22-point improvement compared to 2024-25.

However, the Flyers are off to a nightmarish start this season with a 5-10-6 record, giving them just 16 points, which are tied for the second fewest in the Eastern Conference.

Tocchet has 11 years of head coaching experience, owns a 334-302-105 record, and has taken teams to the playoffs on three occasions.

He also spent 11 of his 18 seasons as a player with the Flyers, but that has not prevented fans from expressing their unhappiness with the direction of the team.

As pressure continues to mount, it is fair to wonder how much more it will take before Brière feels like he has to make a change.

articles.title: Omar Pérez lanza dardo a la Federación tras salida de su hijo de la Selección Colombia y su fichaje por Argentina
articles.standfirst: La fuerte reacción de Omar Pérez tras la polémica exclusión de su hijo en Colombia
articles.summary: La fuerte reacción de Omar Pérez tras la polémica exclusión de su hijo en Colombia
articles.body: El fútbol formativo sudamericano suele estar rodeado de historias de pasión, talento y, en ocasiones, de intrigas administrativas que trascienden el terreno de juego. Recientemente, un episodio acaparó los titulares deportivos a nivel continental involucrando a Franco Pérez, joven mediocampista de las divisiones inferiores de Boca Juniors, y a su padre, el histórico ídolo de Independiente Santa Fe, Omar Pérez. Lo que pintaba como un hito de orgullo nacional para el combinado tricolor terminó convirtiéndose en una novela de decisiones polémicas, silencios institucionales y un rápido giro hacia el combinado argentino. La historia comenzó a tejerse cuando el cuerpo técnico de la Selección Colombia juvenil (encabezado por César Torres) puso los ojos en Franco Pérez, un volante ofensivo de 18 años nacido en Medellín, con doble nacionalidad y un rendimiento destacable en la reserva del club 'xeneize'. El jugador, con sus papeles en regla y una gran ilusión, fue incluido en la primera lista de convocados para un microciclo de preparación y un torneo amistoso de cara al Campeonato Sudamericano Sub-20. Incluso, reportes de la prensa indicaban que ya tenía los tiquetes aéreos listos para viajar a Bogotá. Sin embargo, el escenario dio un giro drástico e inesperado en cuestión de horas. En una segunda versión de la convocatoria publicada por la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol, el nombre de Franco Pérez había desaparecido por completo. La entidad no emitió ningún comunicado oficial ni ofreció explicaciones detalladas que justificaran la baja del volante. Este vacío informativo desató una ola de especulaciones en los medios de comunicación. Periodistas especializados y analistas apuntaron a que la decisión no respondía a un criterio estrictamente futbolístico o a una baja de rendimiento. Por el contrario, se filtraron versiones que señalaban posibles roces dirigenciales o tensiones institucionales indirectas vinculadas a su padre, Omar Pérez, debido a su supuesta relación con proyectos o torneos alternativos no avalados formalmente por el ente rector del balompié colombiano. Ante el revuelo mediático y el duro golpe anímico para el joven futbolista —quien en su momento se limitó a publicar un mensaje reflexivo en sus redes sociales citando pasajes bíblicos—, la respuesta de su padre no tardó en llegar. Omar Pérez utilizó sus plataformas digitales para respaldar públicamente a su hijo. Con un mensaje cargado de emotividad, el 'Diez' dejó entrever su postura frente a las adversidades que rodearon el proceso: "Tu felicidad siempre es la mía, pa. ¡Seguí creciendo, animal! Todo sacrificio tiene recompensa. ¡Que nada ni nadie te quite eso! Te amo mi loco", escribió Omar acompañado de una fotografía de Franco vistiendo los colores de la selección. La frase "que nada ni nadie te quite eso" fue interpretada por los seguidores y la prensa como una clara indirecta hacia las sombras dirigenciales que habrían provocado la marginación del joven en el entorno de la Selección Colombia. La incertidumbre de Franco Pérez duró poco tiempo. Ante la evidente vitrina que significa brillar en el fútbol argentino y el talento demostrado en la reserva de Boca (donde acumula minutos importantes, goles y asistencias), la Asociación del Fútbol Argentino (AFA) actuó con rapidez. El director técnico de la Selección Argentina Sub-20, Diego Placente, decidió convocar al mediocampista colombo-argentino para sumarse de inmediato a los entrenamientos en el predio Lionel Andrés Messi en Ezeiza. Este movimiento representa un punto de inflexión estratégico: Elegibilidad abierta: Al tratarse de un ciclo de entrenamientos y amistosos juveniles, las normativas de la FIFA permiten que el jugador aún mantenga su elegibilidad futura, aunque acerca formalmente al volante a la órbita de la Albiceleste. Revancha deportiva: Para Franco, la convocatoria representa una vía rápida de sanación anímica tras el mal trago vivido en el país cafetero, permitiéndole demostrar sus capacidades bajo la lupa de los campeones del mundo.

articles.title: Llaneros abandona Villavicencio y anuncia su nueva casa para 2027
articles.standfirst: Llaneros confirma su traslado a Guamal para la temporada 2027
articles.summary: Llaneros confirma su traslado a Guamal para la temporada 2027
articles.body: El fútbol profesional colombiano sacudió sus cimientos con un anuncio que marca un antes y un después en la historia reciente de la "Media Colombia". Después de trece años de arraigo ininterrumpido en la capital del departamento del Meta, Llaneros Fútbol Club confirmó de manera oficial su intención de abandonar Villavicencio a partir de la temporada 2027 para trasladar su localía al municipio de Guamal. La noticia, revelada por el presidente de la institución, Juan Carlos Trujillo, encendió el debate en el rentado nacional y expuso las profundas tensiones administrativas que existen entre los clubes profesionales y las entidades públicas encargadas del manejo de los principales escenarios deportivos del país. Las razones de fondo: roces institucionales y costos de operación La decisión de mudar al equipo no responde a un capricho deportivo, sino a una acumulación de tensiones insostenibles con las autoridades locales. Durante los últimos meses, la relación entre las directivas de Llaneros y el Instituto de Deporte y Recreación del Meta (IDERMETA) se fracturó notablemente. Los desacuerdos giraron principalmente en torno a: Los costos de alquiler y uso: Disputas económicas recurrentes por la tarifa y las condiciones comerciales para la utilización del estadio Bello Horizonte-Rey Pelé. Cruces públicos en redes sociales: La tensión escaló a nivel mediático con discusiones directas entre el presidente del club y funcionarios locales, como el director de IDERMETA, Leonardo Ibáñez. Autonomía operativa: Las directivas del club sintieron que no existían las garantías suficientes para la sostenibilidad financiera del proyecto en la máxima categoría del fútbol colombiano, lo que aceleró la búsqueda de nuevos horizontes. Irónicamente, esta salida se da desde un escenario que fue testigo de su época dorada: el Bello Horizonte-Rey Pelé, un estadio modernizado con inversiones superiores a los 90.000 millones de pesos, donde el club celebró el anhelado ascenso a la primera división en 2024 tras años de lucha en la segunda categoría. Guamal, el nuevo hogar y los retos de infraestructura Ante este panorama, la directiva apostó por un cambio geográfico estratégico hacia Guamal, municipio situado a aproximadamente 40 minutos de Villavicencio. El propio Juan Carlos Trujillo confirmó que la Dimayor ya fue notificada de la intención del cambio y conoce formalmente la propuesta. Para cumplir con los estrictos requerimientos reglamentarios de la División Mayor del Fútbol Colombiano de cara a la Liga BetPlay 2027, el proyecto contempla un plan de modernización de la Villa Olímpica de Guamal, un escenario que actualmente cuenta con limitaciones de capacidad —como una estructura reducida a una sola tribuna occidental— y que requerirá intervenciones urgentes. Inicio de obras: Las adecuaciones estructurales y estéticas están programadas para arrancar de manera oficial el próximo 1 de diciembre. Apuesta comunitaria y turística: El club ha presentado proyecciones visuales (renders) que integran la identidad blanquiazul del equipo con los atractivos naturales y la hospitalidad de la región guamaluna, buscando generar un fuerte sentido de pertenencia en los aficionados locales. Un panorama complejo para los estadios en Colombia El caso de Llaneros no es un hecho aislado, sino que refleja una crisis sistémica en el balompié nacional con el uso y la administración de los estadios. Durante el transcurso de las recientes temporadas, equipos históricos como Independiente Santa Fe y Millonarios han tenido que lidiar con la falta de disponibilidad de sus plazas habituales debido a conciertos masivos, gramados en mal estado o diferencias contractuales con los entes gubernamentales. Para Llaneros, el reto de cara al 2027 será doble: consolidar su proyecto deportivo en la primera división —lejos de la zona de descenso y buscando su primera clasificación a los cuadrangulares— y garantizar que su nueva casa en Guamal esté lista a tiempo para albergar el rentado nacional sin contratiempos logísticos.

articles.title: Locura en Premier Padel: otras semifinales con sorpresas
articles.standfirst: Tres parejas fuera del top-8 pelearán por estar en la final del P1 de Dubái
articles.summary: Tres parejas fuera del top-8 pelearán por estar en la final del P1 de Dubái
articles.body: Sin Coello y Tapia ni Chingotto y Galán, la locura se ha apoderado de Premier Padel. Solamente Lebrón y Augsburger se han salvado de la escabechina del P1 de Dubái, donde tres parejas fuera del top-8 han logrado colarse en semifinales. Lo mismo pasó en Kuwait y esta semana ha vuelto a repetirse, en un fiel reflejo de la igualdad que reina en la zona media del circuito. Arrancaron Juan y Leo frente a Maxi Arce y Juan Tello, que se están jugando su presencia en el Tour Finals. Ya lo tuvieron complicado en su debut y nuevamente han sufrido. Son los únicos que han ganado de los favoritos, pero sudando para derrotar a los argentinos. Sin embargo, arrancaron 6-3 arriba en el marcador, algo que no les pasó ante Pol Hernández y Manu Castaño. Todo cambió en la segunda manga, con más errores de Augsburger y con Tello y Arce aprovechándolo. Pusieron otro 6-3 que lo mandaba todo al tercero. Ahí tiraron de galones los número tres para cerrar su billete a semifinales con un 6-2 que disipó las dudas, abriendo una oportunidad de oro para sumar un título juntos, algo que no logran desde el P2 de Bruselas a comienzos de temporada. Jugarán contra una de las revelaciones del último tramo del curso: la dupla formada por Flavio Abbate y Franco Dal Bianco. El primero, italiano, zurdo y con un talento que apunta muy alto, ya dio la campanada en Madrid y sigue creciendo con el objetivo de hacerse un hueco en la zona noble de Premier Padel, algo que ningún compatriota suyo ha conseguido todavía. Su compañero, en cambio, es el ex número uno de A1 Pádel; su nivel ya se conocía, pero el salto al circuito qatarí le estaba costando. Para seguir con su histórico camino esta semana eliminaron a Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo, que continúan con su mala racha de resultados y suman otra oportunidad desperdiciada. El primer set, que se decidió en el tie-break, fue determinante con un 7-6 para Abbate y Dal Bianco. Luego le dieron la vuelta el brasileño y el malagueño con un 6-3, pero lo cerraron Franco y Flavio con un 6-2 que completa su machada. Por el otro lado del cuadro hubo también sorpresas. La principal fue la derrota de Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk. No solo por el hecho de caer en sí, sino por las circunstancias en las que llega. Lo tenían todo para alcanzar la final y soñar con un título: tras un inicio de proyecto con dudas, se afianzaron con dos finales ante Coello y Tapia que les llenaron de confianza, pero en Dubái, con un camino a priori más sencillo, han caído en cuartos. No pudieron superar a Javi Garrido y Juani De Pascual, quienes transmiten muy buenas sensaciones desde que juegan juntos pese a partir fuera de los primeros puestos en los torneos. Pasaron por encima del ‘DJ’ y el ‘Chaqueño’ con un 6-1 en el primer set que rompió todos los pronósticos. El segundo iba por el mismo camino, pero una insuficiente reacción de los número cuatro hizo que terminara con un 7-5 que no cambia el destino final: Javi y Juani estarán en semifinales. Cierran el cupo Gonza Alfonso y Tino Libaak. La pareja que cayó en el tercer partido de la final del Mundial se lleva una alegría una semana después tras tumbar en un partido dificilísimo a Jairo Bautista y Lucas Bergamini, que dieron su brazo a torcer en el tercer set con un 4-6, 6-4 y 7-6 que evidencia la batalla vivida en la pista central.

articles.title: New NHL Trade Rumors on Penguins' Erik Karlsson, Hurricanes Links amid Pittsburgh's Struggles
articles.summary: The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun feels the Carolina Hurricanes will be a likely trade suitor for veteran defenseman Erik Karlsson should the Pittsburgh Penguins shop him this winter.
articles.body:
The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun feels the Carolina Hurricanes will be a likely trade suitor for veteran defenseman Erik Karlsson should the Pittsburgh Penguins shop him this winter.

LeBrun pointed out Friday the Hurricanes were a final candidate in the 2023 race to acquire Karlsson, which ended with the San Jose Sharks trading him to Pittsburgh.

"And I strongly believe the Hurricanes will come calling again on Karlsson once the Penguins decide it's time to formally open up his trade market, which I suspect won't be until the new year," LeBrun reported.

Karlsson will turn 37 in May. He is set to hit unrestricted free agency after playing out the final year of his $11.5 million AAV contract , $1.5 million of which is being paid by the Sharks.

He holds a full no-movement clause on the deal, according to PuckPedia .

Karlsson recorded 66 points (15 goals, 51 assists) in 75 games last season, the highest production total since his 2022-23 Norris Trophy campaign with the Sharks, while helping the Penguins snap a three-year postseason drought.

He has kept that production up with another point-per-game campaign despite frequently rotating defensive partners on a struggling Pittsburgh blue line.

Karlsson currently leads the Penguins with 19 points (three goals, 16 assists) during a 7-10-2 start to the season that has left his team 27th in the NHL standings heading into Friday.

The Hurricanes have started out their Stanley Cup defense by climbing atop the Metropolitan Division standings with a 15-3-2 start to the campaign.

The Canes currently have Jalen Chatfield, Sean Walker and Alexander Nikishin playing on the right side of their defense, which has allowed an NHL-low 22 shots against per game so far this season.

The team could theoretically look to offer one of those players to the Penguins in exchange in order to both bolster their trade offer and clear up a spot for Karlsson. Chatfield is also on track to hit unrestricted free agency, while Nikishin is a pending RFA.

The Canes could then hope Karlsson would offer a boost on offense, particularly on the power play, where the team has ranked 14th in the NHL with a 22.7 percent success rate so far this season.

When discussing the potential trade LeBrun brought up the Hurricanes' interest in another offensive defenseman in John Carlson, who was traded to the Anaheim Ducks at the 2026 deadline in exchange for a conditional 2026 or 2027 first-rounder alongside a 2027 third-round pick.

Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas might hope that deal for Carlson, who was 36 and a pending RFA at the time, will serve as a benchmark as to what his team might get for Karlsson should the franchise shift its focus from trying to make another playoff run with Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin to stocking up on draft capital instead.

articles.title: Kiah Stokes says fans are taking Angel Reese's trash talk 'way too personal' after WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Golden State Valkyries star Kiah Stokes does not seem bothered by Angel Reese's trash talk during the 2026 WNBA Finals.
articles.body: Golden State Valkyries star Kiah Stokes does not seem bothered by Angel Reese's trash talk during the 2026 WNBA Finals. After winning the championship against the Atlanta Dream, Golden State players and staff brought back Reese's famous "too small" gesture during their celebration. However, Stokes believes fans are taking the exchange too seriously. Speaking on Unsupervised, she said trash talk is part of basketball and there is no reason to turn it into a personal fight. She also praised the fans but asked them not to overthink every exchange.Kiah Stokes Explains Why Golden State Valkyries Players Enjoyed Angel Reese's Trash TalkSpeaking on Unsupervised, Stokes said that fans were taking the players' words too personally. She understood why people enjoyed discussing the rivalry but felt they were making too much out of normal on-court exchanges.She said:"I appreciate that we have a lot of fans. But sometimes I feel like y'all are taking things way too personal.This has literally nothing to do with you, and you're making a whole think piece about it. 'Cause I know for us, Angel wanna talk s***, it is what it is. Like, it's a game, and she was cooking. Like, nobody gonna fault her for that... I think it's just fun. I don't take anything personal...and our rookie was also talking s*** back. I'm like, 'Who doesn't love this,' right? So I think, yeah, I think the fans be doing way too much."Stokes' comments came after a Finals series in which Reese was not afraid to speak her mind.During Game 2, Reese recorded 30 points and 16 rebounds as the Atlanta Dream beat Golden State 79-65. She also exchanged words with rookie Aminata Gueye. At one point, Reese was heard saying, "You can't guard me!"Game 3 brought another exchange. Atlanta won 97-71, and Reese directed a "You bum!" remark and the "too small" gesture toward the Valkyries' bench. She also waved at the players as they left the court.Before Game 4, Reese said she wanted to affect Golden State's confidence and do whatever she could to trouble the team.The exchanges continued in Game 6. After finishing a play through contact against Stokes, Reese turned toward the bench and said, "Sit down, you're on the bench." Atlanta won 80-69 to send the series to a deciding Game 7.However, Golden State had the final say. The Valkyries won 68-63 on October 31 to claim their first WNBA championship. Gabby Williams scored 30 points, including 28 in the second half, and earned Finals MVP honors.valkyries.wnba.com+1Reese's "too small" gesture then became part of Golden State's championship celebrations. Aminata Gueye shared a picture of the gesture after the win, while teammate Tiffany Hayes copied it during an Instagram Live session.The jokes continued at the November 4 championship parade in San Francisco. Some Valkyries staff members wore black shirts featuring Reese's face edited into the Crying Jordan meme alongside the same hand gesture. Former Warriors player and Bay Area analyst Festus Ezeli also held up one of the shirts. Fans were seen carrying pink pacifiers with tags reading "if found return to: ATL."Stokes also joined the celebrations with a shirt that referred to ESPN's preseason title odds, which had not placed Golden State among the top five teams.Her own actions help explain why she sees the exchanges as part of the fun rather than a personal issue.Meanwhile, Reese announced that she was taking a break from her podcast and planned to spend the next six months focusing on herself. She also said Florida would be her home base and that she would share occasional vlogs. She did not connect the decision to the Finals or the parade.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Cena Discusses New Look Since Retirement

Stars Who Could Make Shock Return at Survivor Series 😮

John Cena retired as an active professional wrestler last December, but he has continued to make periodic appearances for WWE, especially lately with regard to the upcoming John Cena Classic.

While Cena still sports a familiar look from his wrestling days with his trademark T-shirt and hat, he has also made a conscious effort to change things up.

Cena explained his line of thinking in an interview with SI.com's Rick Ucchino this week.

"Those weren't jorts in Brooklyn, and they weren't jorts on NXT. I'm wearing cargo shorts," Cena said. "I'm not wearing any wristbands, I don't have a towel and I don't have any knee pads. So, when I said the jorts are retired, the f----ing jorts are retired. ...

"I don't wanna confuse the consumer. If I show up in dress shoes in a suit with a pocket watch, hopefully the consumer isn't gonna think one more match. John's not really done. That didn't work. They still chanted one more match. And I love wearing suits. Also, Cody Rhodes gets beat up in suits. So, the one thing I was trying to accomplish was really murky."

Cena had the final match of his legendary career on Saturday Night's Main Event, which took place on Dec. 13, 2025.

While Cena tapped out in a loss to Gunther, much to the chagrin of a large portion of the WWE Universe, he still received a heartwarming send-off from WWE Superstars and the fans.

Cena remains an important part of the WWE family as an ambassador, and he has been front and center lately as the face of the John Cena Classic.

The 17-time world champion has invited several WWE main roster and NXT Superstars to participate for a chance to become the first John Cena Classic champion, including Cody Rhodes.

Cena will undoubtedly be on hand for the John Cena Classic when it takes place at the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex in Orlando, Florida, on Dec. 14.

Amid rumors of WWE Hall of Famer Shawn Michaels eventually assuming Bruce Prichard's role on WWE's main roster as creative director, new details have emerged regarding what that could mean for NXT.

According to PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ), CM Punk is viewed as the person most likely to succeed Michaels if and when he makes the move from NXT to the main roster.

Punk has reportedly been present for the "majority" of NXT television tapings in recent weeks, and he is being "prepped" to take over Michaels' position.

As for WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles, PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ) reports that WWE wants to use him as a scout for the WWE ID program rather than as Michaels' replacement.

PWInsider did note that Styles has been more involved with NXT lately as a producer, though, due in part to Terry Taylor's absence after undergoing knee surgery.

Last month, PWInsider.com's Mike Johnson was the first to report that Prichard is expected to step down from his position after WrestleMania 43 in order to work more from home.

Johnson added at the time that Michaels was considered Prichard's most likely replacement.

There is little doubt that NXT would be in good hands in the event that Punk and Styles take on bigger roles once Michaels departs, but it is fair to wonder if Punk can or will be in NXT full time while he continues to wrestle.

At 48 years of age, Punk is in the latter stages of his career, but he continues to wrestle at a high level and appears to have plenty left in the tank.

Should Punk be the direct replacement for Michaels, it could require him to scale back on his wrestling or perhaps even retire in the near future.

That would be a big loss for WWE programming, but Punk's credentials speak for themselves when it comes to his fit as head of NXT.

WWE's Reported Plans for Gunther vs. Balor

WWE is reportedly still planning a match between Gunther and Finn Balor despite it not taking place last weekend at Crown Jewel.

According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t WrestlePurists ), Gunther vs. Balor was originally planned for Crown Jewel, but it did not take place despite shooting angles for it.

However, Gunther vs. Balor is reportedly still planned to happen at a later date, although it isn't clear when.

Meltzer added that Gunther vs. Balor was removed from Crown Jewel because Gunther decided against traveling to Saudi Arabia for the show amid the recent conflict with Yemen.

Over the past several weeks, Gunther and Balor have had several altercations on SmackDown, including the Halloween-themed episode on Oct. 30 when Balor showed up as The Demon and attacked The Ring General.

Given how long-running the feud between Gunther and Balor has been, there is little doubt that they will settle the score at some point.

The only question relates to whether it will happen on an episode of SmackDown or at an upcoming premium live event such as Survivor Series or Wrestlepalooza.

articles.title: Joshua Kimmich proud of Germany’s “thoroughly deserved win” against Serbia
articles.summary: Three goals, three points, and third spot in Group B.
articles.body:
Germany produced a strong first-half showing against Serbia. Jürgen Klopp's men applied pressure early, forcing an own goal from left-back Srđan Babić after just three minutes of play. Florian Wirtz doubled Germany's lead 11 minutes later. Klopp's side finished the first half two goals to the good.

Germany picked up where they left off at the start of the second half, with Brajan Gruda scoring his first-ever goal for the national team in the 50th minute. However, Serbia would strike back. Just six minutes later, Babić made up for his first-half mistake by scoring — on the correct side of the field this time. Germany walked away with a largely dominant, 3-1 victory.

But don't let the scoreline fool you. After Serbia's goal, the match became chaotic, and according to Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, created a few problems for his side.

"I thought the first half was very good," said Kimmich (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). "I think we played some good football. We had a few problems after the break, and things became a little hectic. Serbia played a lot of long balls, and the pitch also became difficult to play on towards the end. Nevertheless, it was a thoroughly deserved win. We could have scored a few more goals, but we'll take the 3-1."

Germany face Netherlands next in a winner-takes-all encounter on November 16. A win against Xavi Hernández's flying Dutchmen will guarantee Die Mannschaft a spot in the Nations League Quarter-final.

articles.title: Dolphins Rookie Chris Bell Doubtful For Week 10 After Knee Setback
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins rookie Chris Bell is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Colts. See the injury details and what it means for Kyle McCord.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins face a tough test this Sunday, and their injury list just got longer. Rookie wide receiver Chris Bell is listed as doubtful for the Week 10 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. This news comes right before quarterback Kyle McCord prepares to make his first career start. The timing could not be worse for a team that already struggles to score points.

Bell suffered a hit to the same knee that required surgery before he even joined the NFL causing a new knee issue. Head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed the status on Friday, stating the team does not view the issue as a long-term problem. Yet, the immediate impact on the roster is clear. Bell missed the second practice of the week at the Baptist Health Training Complex. He was downgraded from limited participation to no practice at all on Thursday.

Chris Bell entered the league with a lot of hope, but his path has been rocky. Before his draft selection, the 22-year-old receiver's college career concluded due to a torn ACL. He has worked hard to get back on the field, catching 12 passes for 148 yards in his first eight games. Those numbers show promise, but they are not enough to fill a gap if he sits out. According to Yahoo Sports , the team downgraded his status after seeing how his knee reacted to contact.

The Dolphins need every able body right now. The team holds a 1-7 record after losing to the Detroit Lions on Sunday. With the offense already sputtering, losing a rookie who is just finding his rhythm hurts the chances of a comeback. McCord will have to rely on older veterans if Bell cannot go. The pressure on the young quarterback just went up a notch.

The Dolphins travel to Lucas Oil Stadium to face the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. This is a road game that demands a full team effort. A 1-7 squad cannot afford to play short-handed against the rival. The coaching staff has to decide if Bell is too risky to play. Hafley said the injury is not long-term, but the doubtful tag means he is unlikely to see the field. Per Yahoo Sports, the team announced the designation after Bell failed to practice fully.

Every week matters for a team trying to avoid a historic collapse. The loss to Detroit showed the team lacks depth and consistency. Now, the absence of a key rookie adds another layer of difficulty. The Colts will look to exploit any weakness in the Dolphins' receiving corps. If Bell sits, the passing game loses a fresh set of eyes and legs.

The Dolphins have to hope Bell recovers quickly. The coach believes the knee issue will not keep him out for the season. But Sunday is a different story. The team must move forward with the players they have. Kyle McCord will lead the offense without the benefit of a healthy rookie receiver. The game starts at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 15.

articles.title: Braves Lock Up Evan Phillips For Bullpen Depth
articles.summary: The Atlanta Braves signed Evan Phillips to a premium deal. Battery Power reports the stats show he is healthy and ready for 2027.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves just wrote another check for relief pitching, and they did not blink. Evan Phillips is coming to town after the team paid a premium price to secure his arm. The signing of Evan Phillips shocks no one who has watched the front office spend big on late-inning arms in recent years. According to Battery Power , the signing came out of nowhere, arriving as a bolt from the blue for fans who expected rotation help instead.

Atlanta needed a fix because Raisel Iglesias is still a free agent with no guarantee of a return. The club cannot rely on hope when it comes to closing games. They need proven arms that can handle the pressure of the eighth and ninth innings. Battery Power notes that if Iglesias does return, it will likely be on a one-year deal, leaving the team to add even more talent to the mix. The team must build a bullpen that can dominate late in games.

Everyone asked if Phillips could stay on the mound after missing most of 2025 and 2026 with injuries. The answer is yes, and the numbers prove his stuff is back to elite levels. With a 97 mph fastball in 2026, he ranked in the 85th percentile for velocity among all pitchers. Battery Power reports he also posted a 31.1 percent strikeout rate while keeping his walk rate down to just 5.7 percent.

His secondary pitches show the same dominance that made him a star before his Tommy John surgery. His sweeper sat at 86 mph, three miles per hour above the average for right-handers. The cutter hit 93 mph, also three miles above average, while his sinker reached 97 mph. These are not just good numbers; they are the marks of a pitcher who can shut down opposing lineups.

Braves fans should feel good about the shape of the bullpen heading into the 2027 season. Dylan Lee and Robert Suarez already anchor the high-leverage spots, and now Phillips joins that group. The team might still bring back Iglesias to form a one-two punch, but the depth is already there.

Relievers are volatile and injuries happen, but the talent level is undeniable. The front office is not playing it safe with a cheap option; they are buying the best available talent on the market. This approach mirrors the aggressive spending that has defined the franchise's recent success. The Braves are set to field a dangerous bullpen if the arms stay healthy.

articles.body:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was handed a 12-match ban on Friday for a serious foul on CD Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel, who died a day after the challenge.

The Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee said the suspension was the maximum punishment allowed under its rules for the offence described in the referee's report.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest following Owono's challenge during a 2-2 draw in Spain's second division on November 2. He was treated on the pitch and carried off on a stretcher before dying in hospital the next day, aged 30.

Owono was sent off for the challenge, which referee Manuel Ángel Pérez Hernández described in his match report as involving excessive force.

Owono, 25, expressed deep distress following de Miguel's death and is receiving psychological and medical support from his club, according to Spanish newspaper Marca.

Andorra coach Carles Manso has dismissed reports that the goalkeeper is considering retirement.

articles.summary: Pacers forward Aaron Nesmith was originally listed as questionable for Friday's game but Indiana got good news ahead of game vs Knicks
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Forward Aaron Nesmith will be available for the Indiana Pacers' game against the New York Knicks , the team announced ahead of the game on social media.

Nesmith was previously listed as questionable for Friday's game after he left Wednesday's win over the Washington Wizards with right knee soreness. When asked pregame on Friday if Nesmith would play, head coach Rick Carlisle said "hope so."

Nesmith played 22 minutes on Wednesday, scoring just two points on 1-of-6 shooting. It was his lowest-scoring game of the season so far.

T.J. McConnell, who was listed as probable, will also be available for the Pacers on Friday night. Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring), Johnny Furphy (ACL tear), and Ben Sheppard (meniscus) remain out.

articles.title: The Boston Celtics have overcome an issue that previously haunted them
articles.summary: For the first time in a long time, cold stretches from deep aren't leading to losses
articles.body:
In previous years, the Boston Celtics would find themselves in a tough situation on nights when their three-point shot wasn't falling. We saw it under Brad Stevens, Ime Udoka and Joe Mazzulla. The Celtics would often double down on trying to shoot themselves out of a slump, usually to their detriment.

However, to begin the 2026-27 NBA season, Boston has showcased a varied offense. As a result, the Celtics have become tougher to beat and are no longer beholden to the whims of shot variance. Even when their perimeter looks aren't falling, Mazzulla's team is adjusting on the fly and figuring out different ways to win games, which is something Celtics fans have been calling for over the past few years.

Following the Celtics' latest road trip, which saw them go 4-0, including an impressive win over the Philadelphia 76ers , the 'First To The Floor' podcast broke down the different ways Boston is winning games and why the versatility in its approach will be so important moving forward.

articles.title: Dissecting the Boston Celtics 4-0 road trip
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics went 4-0 on their latest road trip, climbing to first in the East as a result
articles.body:
After 12 games, the Boston Celtics sit at the top of the Eastern Conference with a 10-2 record. Joe Mazzulla's team has just navigated a four-game road trip, winning every matchup, including a tough back-to-back against the Philadelphia 76ers and the Toronto Raptors . Jayson Tatum has begun to find his rhythm when shooting from deep after a tough start to the campaign.

Of course, we're still early in the new NBA season, and the Celtics will face some tough challenges in the weeks and months ahead. Nevertheless, there's no denying how quickly the Celtics have hit the ground running following a summer that saw the departure of Jaylen Brown.

Following the Celtics impressive come-from-behind win over the Raptors on Wednesday, August 11, Jack Simone and Sam LaFrance discussed Boston's strong road trip in the latest episode of their 'How 'Bout Them Celtics?' podcast. The duo shared their thoughts on Tatum's game-changing performance in Toronto, along with Derrick White showing signs of a bounce-back season after struggling in the 2025-26 campaign.
